Heading: Editorial | Delayed Honor for Martyrs: Damage to Government's Credibility
Summary: The article criticizes the Central Government for its significant delay in officially acknowledging the martyrdom of six soldiers in 'Operation Sindoor', which came to light over a year after the incident. It argues that this lack of transparency, coupled with conflicting statements from officials including the Defense Minister, undermines democratic values and public trust. The editorial emphasizes that a democratic government must be transparent about national losses and setbacks, rather than concealing facts or creating false narratives, as failures are inherent in a humane system.
Content: It is unfortunate that the Central Government has revealed the martyrdom of six soldiers in 'Operation Sindoor' with extreme delay. This behavior signifies the government's failure to uphold the best democratic values of transparency and open-mindedness. The names of Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh, Sergeant Surendra Kumar, and Agniveer Mood Muralinayak have been engraved on the '3-D' section of the 'Tyagchakra' wall at the National War Memorial in Delhi. This information came to light on June 26. It is commendable that the soldiers who sacrificed their lives for the country have been remembered and honored, even if it is more than a year after 'Operation Sindoor'. Every soldier who fought and sacrificed their life for the country deserves national honor. However, the delay in officially recording the names and identities of these six martyrs raises doubts about the government's transparency and the credibility of its statements, and the explanation provided by the government in this regard is unsatisfactory. In May 2025, the then Director General of Military Operations (DGMO), Lieutenant General Rajeev Ghai, had stated that there were casualties in 'Operation Sindoor'. However, he did not disclose the names of the soldiers the country lost. Air Chief Marshal A.P. Singh, Chief of Air Staff, had met Sergeant Surendra Kumar's family; gallantry awards were also given to the families of the martyrs. Despite this, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh had clearly stated in the Lok Sabha that no Indian soldier was harmed during 'Operation Sindoor'. It is now being argued that the minister had only denied a report related to the death of a pilot, and this explanation is not believable. A situation has now arisen where Defense Minister Rajnath Singh may face a privilege motion in the Lok Sabha for providing false information. The government's refusal to disclose details about the casualties in the operation needs to be examined in light of the statements made by military officials regarding the losses incurred in the operation. During 'Operation Balakot' in 2019, military officials had also stated that all Indian aircraft and pilots had returned safely. However, the government later had to admit that Wing Commander Abhinandan Varthaman was captured in Pakistan. No one expects the government or the military to disclose operational details and other confidential information related to conflicts. However, in a democratic system, the government must be transparent in providing information about the losses and setbacks the country has experienced. False narratives should not be created by concealing or exaggerating facts. The government gains public trust only when it is open and accountable to the people. The government's behavior of selectively disclosing truths and facts, its statements, and its assertions create distrust among the people. The greatness of democracy does not lie in portraying itself as a superhuman force or a system that makes no mistakes. Democracy is a very humane system, and failures are natural within it. Concealing facts and failures weakens democracy rather than strengthening it.

Heading: 6 Soldiers Who Challenged Pakistan
Summary: The article details 'Operation Sindoor', a retaliatory precision strike by India against Pakistani terrorist camps, launched after 26 tourists were killed by Pakistani terrorists in Pahalgam, Kashmir. The Indian Air Force and Army targeted 9 camps, killing over a hundred terrorists and damaging military bases, leading to a Pakistani ceasefire request. The report also honors 6 Indian soldiers who attained martyrdom during this operation, whose names are now inscribed on the National War Memorial in Delhi, with some having received gallantry awards.
Content:
Operation Sindoor proved that the valor of Indian soil is second to none, amazing the whole world. In beautiful Kashmir, there is a green valley called Pahalgam, a popular tourist destination accessible only by horse or on foot, often considered a paradise for newly married couples. Last year, on April 22, five Pakistani terrorists suddenly emerged from a nearby forest with automatic weapons and indiscriminately attacked tourists, killing 26 people while sparing women. One victim was a local horse rider. In retaliation for this brutal act, which caused the wives of the deceased to lose their kumkum, the Indian government launched 'Operation Sindoor'.

In the early hours of May 7, India carried out a precision strike on terrorist camps in Pakistan. The Indian Air Force and Army targeted nine terrorist camps within Pakistan from Indian borders, killing over a hundred terrorists and damaging several Pakistani airbases and military installations using missiles and modern weapons. Unable to withstand the attack, Pakistan requested a ceasefire, which India announced on the evening of May 10. During this operation, details of six Indian soldiers who attained martyrdom were recently released for the first time: five from the Army and one from the Air Force. Army soldier Sunil Kumar was awarded the 'Vir Chakra' and Air Force Sergeant Surendra Kumar received the 'Vayu Sena' medal last year. The names of Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Soldier Murali Naik, and Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh have also been officially announced and are slated for awards. Their names are inscribed on the National War Memorial in Delhi, and the entire nation pays tribute to these heroes. Their heroic deeds and sacrifices for the nation should be remembered by future generations whenever Operation Sindoor is mentioned. India will never forget their sacrifice, and their families should receive all necessary assistance. The sacrifice of these six soldiers will forever be etched in the pages of history alongside Operation Sindoor.

Heading: Ayodhya Temple Trust Donation Fraud: K.C. Venugopal Demands Supreme Court-Monitored Investigation
Summary: K.C. Venugopal, MP and Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee, has demanded a Supreme Court-monitored investigation into alleged donation fraud and financial irregularities in the Ayodhya Sree Rama Temple Trust, calling it the "biggest temple robbery" in the country. He criticized the BJP for its silence and accused authorities of protecting high-ranking culprits while implicating lower-level staff. Additionally, Venugopal announced a privilege motion against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh for allegedly misleading Parliament regarding soldier injuries in Operation Sindoor, accusing national media of suppressing these critical issues.
Content:
NEW DELHI | K.C. Venugopal MP, Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee, demanded that an independent agency investigate the alleged donation fraud and financial irregularities amounting to crores of rupees in the Ayodhya Sree Rama Temple Trust, under the supervision of the Supreme Court. Venugopal stated that he has sent a letter to the Prime Minister requesting this. He was speaking at a press conference in Delhi. He pointed out that what happened in Ayodhya is the biggest temple robbery in the country. The BJP, which has used Ayodhya as a political weapon for thirty years, is now unwilling to utter a word about this massive robbery that has affected the sentiments of crores of devotees, and this has exposed the true face of those who preach great devotion and patriotism in the country, K.C. Venugopal stated.

The allegation that donations, including money and gold, submitted by crores of devotees across the country have been plundered is extremely serious. Preliminary investigations reveal the activities of an organized fraud syndicate. Venugopal alleged that money and valuable ornaments were stolen daily, and crucial CCTV footage was destroyed. Complaints from the Trust's former Chief Accounts Officer, who warned about financial irregularities in 2020-21, were ignored, and he was removed from his job. Even when the State Bank of India recently pointed out irregularities in donation counting, necessary action was not taken.

K.C. Venugopal questioned the credibility of the Special Investigation Team formed by the Uttar Pradesh government and the current investigation procedures, expressing concern that efforts are being made to protect the high-ranking real culprits who led the fraud by implicating only lower-level officials. He alleged that despite the temple being under the full control of the central government, when the fraud came to light, only poor, lower-level employees were made accused, protecting the real culprits.

Under the leadership of Uttar Pradesh Congress President Ajay Rai, the Congress staged a strong protest on this issue. There was even a situation where Ajay Rai was placed under house arrest in Ayodhya. People worship Sree Rama as a symbol of justice and righteousness. Trying to cover up such a massive corruption that occurred in such a holy land is a grave injustice to the devotees.

K.C. Venugopal also stated that a privilege motion has been moved against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh for misleading the Lok Sabha by stating that no soldiers were injured in Operation Sindoor. Despite soldiers suffering casualties and injuries, the Union Minister adopted a stance that deceived the people of the country on a matter related to national security. He also alleged that national media are deliberately suppressing important issues like the Ayodhya robbery and the privilege motion against the Union Minister. However, K.C. Venugopal clarified that the Congress and the INDIA alliance will continue their united fight to strongly raise these issues.

Heading: BJP gears up to face NEET paper leak, Ram mandir fund theft in upcoming Monsoon session amid shift in power dynamics
Summary: The BJP is preparing to address significant challenges, including the NEET paper leak and the Ram Temple donation scam, during the upcoming Monsoon Session of Parliament. This session, expected to run from late July to mid-August, will also see major shifts in power dynamics due to party defections. The government aims to pass key legislations, such as the 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill and a bill to criminalize narcotics consumption, while also potentially revisiting the delimitation bill.
Content:
New Delhi: The RamTemple donation scam, re-NEET as well as the casualties of Operation Sindoor are going to be some of the key heckling points the BJP is preparing to face in the upcoming Monsoon Session, even as power dynamics and seating arrangements are set for a major uphaul. The defection from several parties will not just alter the dynamics but will also be a key flashpoint between the treasury benches and the Opposition.

Government sources have indicated that the Session could start either on July 20 or July 27, and is likely to go on till August 13.

The BJP is keen to pass some important legislations, including the 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill as well as a legislation to criminalise the consumption of narcotics. Last session, its key legislation, the delimitation bill fell through after it could not cobble up the two-thirds numbers it needed.

Sources said that the 130th Constitutional Amendment Bill, which seeks to remove ministers including the PM and CMs after 30 days of detention and arrests, could be used as a litmus test by the government to gauge numbers. If indeed it has the numbers, the government will not miss an opportunity to pass the delimitation bill this session. A key minister had indicated to reporters that if the need arises, the government was ready to bring in a Special Session to see through the legislation’s passage even before the Monsoon Session.

The upcoming session will also see a huge change in power dynamics with parties like the AAP, TMC and Shiv Sena (UBT) facing defections, and the NCP (SP) likely to merge either with the NDA or the Congress. Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla is yet to take a final call on the rebels of TMC and Shiv Sena (UBT) seeking recognition as separate groups.

The Opposition will have far lesser strength than they had earlier. The Congress’s possible fallout with the DMK, too, will play out especially after the Dravidian party has asked for a separate sitting arrangement from the Congress.

Heading: Congress preparing to bring privilege motion against Defense Minister, what is the whole matter?
Summary: Congress MP K.C. Venugopal is preparing to move a privilege motion against Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of misleading Parliament regarding casualties in 'Operation Sindoor'. Venugopal claims Singh initially stated no soldiers were injured, but now 6 martyrs are announced, calling it a grave insult to the army and their families. He asserts that concealing information from the House is a breach of privilege and has requested the Lok Sabha Speaker to initiate proceedings.
Content: Privilege Motion against Rajnath Singh: K.C. Venugopal has leveled serious allegations against the Defense Minister for misleading Parliament and the people of the country. Venugopal strongly attacked the BJP government, stating that for them, 'patriotism' and 'devotion to Ram' are merely tools for political gain and hollow slogans. Congress MP K.C. Venugopal claimed a contradiction in the Defense Minister's statements, saying, 'The Defense Minister had previously stated on record in Parliament that not a single soldier was injured in Operation Sindoor. But now it is being said that 6 of our soldiers have been martyred. This is clearly a statement misleading the country and the House, an outright lie. How can the Defense Minister lie in a sacred place like Parliament?' Questioning the central government's intentions, the Congress leader said that in July 2025, the government claimed no Indian soldier was martyred, and now, a year later, the army is announcing the martyrdom of 6 soldiers. He called this a grave insult to the army and the families of the martyrs. K.C. Venugopal said, 'Our brave soldiers sacrificed their lives defending the country from enemies, but the government, which calls itself nationalist, hid their martyrdom and lied to the country. Keeping the people of the country unaware of the bravery and supreme sacrifice of the soldiers is extremely shameful.' Citing parliamentary rules, Venugopal stated that it is an established rule that if a minister conceals information from the House or misleads it, it constitutes a breach of privilege and contempt of the House. On this basis, he has submitted a letter to the Honorable Lok Sabha Speaker, requesting immediate initiation of privilege motion proceedings against the Defense Minister.

Heading: 'Ayodhya land deal is the biggest temple scam the country has ever seen; The trust provided all assistance to those who looted'; K.C. Venugopal against BJP
Summary: Congress leader K.C. Venugopal has accused the Ayodhya land deal of being the country's biggest temple scam, alleging that the BJP and Central government are protecting the real culprits and remaining silent. He called for a Supreme Court-supervised investigation, stating that the Uttar Pradesh government's SIT would be ineffective. Venugopal also criticized the Central government on various other issues, including misleading Parliament on military casualties, errors in CBSE exam center allocation, and the Adani share controversy.
Content: Thiruvananthapuram: Congress leader and MP K.C. Venugopal alleged that the Ayodhya land deal is the biggest temple scam the country has ever seen. He also alleged that the BJP and the Central government are maintaining silence on the issue and are taking a stance of protecting the culprits. The trust appointed by the government led the temple construction on the land provided by the Central government. K.C. Venugopal said that the trust provided all assistance to those who looted, ignoring warnings, and that only ordinary employees are being made accused, protecting the real culprits. He alleged that such a big fraud cannot be carried out by a few employees alone, and that the BJP and the Central government are protecting the main people behind it. He demanded that those who always talk about devotion to Rama are the ones who carried out this looting, and that the Central government should give a clear answer on the issue. He said that the Ayodhya land deal should be investigated under the supervision of the Supreme Court, and that it was an attack on the devotees. K.C. Venugopal also criticized that the special investigation team formed by the Uttar Pradesh government will not be able to find the real culprits. He clarified that the Congress will raise the issue in Parliament and will not let go of the Ayodhya fraud. Meanwhile, K.C. Venugopal also criticized the Central government on the issue of Operation Sindoor. He alleged that the Centre misled Parliament regarding the martyrdom of soldiers, and that the Centre had informed that no one was injured. He also said that there were errors in allocating CBSE examination centers, and that CBSE has informed that an explanation can be given regarding this. He added that a meeting was held with the CBSE and NTA chairpersons regarding the question paper leak, and an explanation was sought regarding the steps taken by the Ministry of Education. K.C. Venugopal also reacted to the Vizhinjam agreement and the Adani share controversy. He said that Adani should respond to this matter, and that Adani cannot make decisions without informing the Kerala government. He also criticized that 'Adani is not a superpower in Kerala like in BJP-ruled states'. K.C. Venugopal also reacted to Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan mentioning his name. His reply was, 'You haven't forgotten my name, you remember it, right?'

Heading: Rajkot Piyush Kumar Murders Partner: Police investigation began after a highly decomposed body, dressed in women's clothes, was found near the Muscat Phatak railway wall.
Summary: A 20-year-old man, Piyush Kumar Kharwar, murdered his partner, Chandan Kumar, after discovering Chandan, who had posed as a woman named 'Nisha Kumar'/'Poonam' on social media, was actually a man. Piyush had believed Chandan was his wife and had even applied sindoor. The highly decomposed body was found on June 25, leading to a police investigation that identified Piyush through CCTV footage, who subsequently confessed to the crime.
Content:
Rajkot Piyush Kumar Murders Partner: Police investigation began after a highly decomposed body, dressed in women's clothes, was found near the Muscat Phatak railway wall.

Ahmedabad: On social media, new relationships are both formed and broken. In Rajkot city, Gujarat, 20-year-old Piyush Kumar Kharwar met a young woman on social media, and a conversation began between them; the woman started considering him her husband. She even applied sindoor in her hair parting in his name. However, as soon as Piyush realized that the person he was communicating with was not actually a woman but a man, he murdered him. The investigation into this case began on June 25. Police found a highly decomposed body, dressed in women's clothes, near the railway wall. Initially, it was considered a case of accidental death; however, the post-mortem report revealed severe head injuries, leading officials to register a murder case and restart the investigation. Police searched for the accused using CCTV footage. They eventually reached 20-year-old Piyush Kumar Kharwar. During police interrogation, Piyush confessed to his crime. According to the police, Piyush came into contact with a person named 'Nisha Kumar' on Facebook and 'Poonam' on Instagram. It was Chandan Kumar who was operating both these accounts. He had adopted a female persona to gain Piyush's trust. Later, Piyush and Chandan, who was actually living as a woman named Poonam, started living together like husband and wife. Chandan avoided physical intimacy, telling Piyush that it was due to religious vows. Piyush had accepted Chandan as his wife and had even applied sindoor in his hair parting as part of a ritual. One day, Piyush saw Chandan shaving, and that's when he understood the truth; he realized that his partner was actually a man who was seeking homosexual relationships. After this revelation, differences between them grew, and Piyush fled, leaving Chandan. However, Chandan tracked Piyush through Uttar Pradesh and Rajasthan and eventually found him at a factory in Padwala, Rajkot. On June 21, an argument broke out between them at Piyush's workplace. According to the police, Piyush then took Chandan to a secluded spot near the railway tracks and committed the murder there. He hid Chandan's body under stones and returned to his work shift. Rajkot Rural Superintendent of Police Vijay Singh Gurjar stated that a murder case has been registered under Section 103(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, and legal proceedings are underway.

Heading: PAC unanimously dissatisfied over lack of Education Department audit since 2017," says KC Venugopal
Summary: The Public Accounts Committee (PAC), led by KC Venugopal, expressed unanimous dissatisfaction regarding the Education Department's lack of a performance audit for the past nine years, since 2017. The committee, while reviewing centrally sponsored welfare schemes, deemed this absence of auditing as disappointing and unjustifiable. Members also raised several questions about these schemes, to which the Ministry of Education provided initial responses.
Content: Congress MP and Public Accounts Committee ( PAC ) Chairperson KC Venugopal on Thursday expressed dissatisfaction over the absence of a performance audit of the Education Department over the past nine years, saying the committee had unanimously raised concerns while reviewing the implementation of centrally sponsored welfare schemes. The PAC met at Parliament House Annexe to examine the implementation and effectiveness of centrally sponsored welfare schemes in the education sector. The meeting included a briefing by the Audit authorities, followed by oral evidence from officials of the Ministry of Education, the Department of School Education and Literacy, and the Department of Higher Education. Speaking to ANI, Venugopal said the committee's primary concern was the lack of a performance audit of the Education Department since 2017. "We are discussing today about the centrally sponsored welfare schemes of the Education Department. We discussed about that. Basically, one of the observations made by the committee in the initial stage itself, that on audit. Because the audit on education was done in 2017 last. Since the last nine years, there is no audit for the Education Department by the audit body. Which is actually disappointing. No, that is not at all disappointing, it is not justifiable also," Venugopal said. Emphasising the importance of education, he added, "Education is one of the important subjects. I think it should be audited properly. Performance audit has not been conducted for the last nine years. So, the committee unanimously found this unsatisfactory. The committee totally showed its dissatisfaction on this issue." Venugopal further said members of the committee also raised several questions regarding centrally sponsored welfare schemes, adding that the Ministry had responded to some of the queries and would provide additional details at a later stage. "Regarding the schemes also, many queries were raised by members about the centrally sponsored schemes. Certainly, the Ministry replied. At the next stage, they will give details," he said. Responding to a question regarding the privilege notice moved against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh over his remarks on Operation Sindoor, Venugopal said, "It's already there, already given to the Speaker and the Speaker has to take a decision." The PAC 's review comes as centrally sponsored welfare programmes, including the recently implemented Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) Act, continue to remain under parliamentary scrutiny over their implementation and effectiveness across the country.

Heading: Suspended lady Kendrapara IIC moves Orissa High Court seeking anticipatory bail in custodial torture case
Summary: Suspended Inspector-in-Charge Sandhyarani Jena has filed for anticipatory bail in the Orissa High Court, facing serious charges of custodial torture against a woman and her son. Allegations include physical assault, criminal intimidation, and extortion, with police finding that CCTV footage was intentionally removed from the station. This incident highlights a persistent pattern of procedural violations by Jena, who has been suspended three times in the past six years.
Content:
Expecting imminent arrest, suspended Inspector-in-Charge (IIC) Sandhyarani Jena filed an anticipatory bail petition before theOrissa High Court. Jena, the former head of the Talachua Marine Police Station in Kendrapara district, was recently suspended following severe allegations of subjecting a woman and her son to third-degree custodial torture.

Following the allegations, a criminal case was formally registered against Jena on June 1, at the Talachua Marine Police Station, reportedly. The police department invoked several serious provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) against the suspended officer.

The statutory charges include Section 74 (assault or use of criminal force against a woman with intent to outrage her modesty), Section 115 (voluntarily causing hurt), Section 351 (criminal intimidation), Section 308 (extortion), and Section 296 (committing obscene acts in a public place).

Fearing arrest under these non-bailable sections, Jena approached the High Court seeking pre-arrest bail, while describing the entire case as a fabricated conspiracy against her.

The controversy stems from an incident on May 25, when the complainants, identified as Annapurna and her son Ananta, visited the Talachua Marine Police Station to lodge a complaint regarding an ongoing family dispute. Instead of receiving assistance, the duo alleged they were subjected to brutal physical abuse inside the station premises.

In her deposition before the Sub-Divisional Police Officer (SDPO), Annapurna alleged that the IIC physically assaulted her, forcibly wiped off her vermilion (sindoor), broke her conch bangles, and hurled verbal abuse. Her son, Ananta, further alleged that Jena and a local Home Guard dragged him into a toilet block, where they strangled and physically assaulted him.

The registration of the criminal case was initiated after the Director General of Police (DGP) ordered an administrative inquiry into the matter. A field assessment conducted by the district Superintendent of Police (SP) and the SDPO revealed that the police station's closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras and recording footage had been intentionally removed to prevent the documentation of the event. These findings were subsequently forwarded to the DGP, who ordered her immediate suspension.

The latest case renewed scrutiny over Jena's professional record, revealing a persistent pattern of procedural violations. The officer has been suspended three times within the past six years due to disciplinary infractions.

In 2020, while serving as the IIC of Patna Police Station inKeonjhardistrict, Jena was suspended after she was caught on camera allegedly assaulting a youth, Raju Mahanta, who had been illegally detained for 25 days over a land dispute.

Four years later, while posted at the Lakhanpur Police Station inJharsugudadistrict, she faced her second suspension in connection with another operational irregularity. While departmental proceedings are underway, the high court's decision on her anticipatory bail will dictate the direction of the criminal trial.

Heading: No one will be spared": UP BJP president Pankaj Chaudhary on SIT crackdown over Ayodhya donation embezzlement
Summary: Uttar Pradesh BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary dismissed opposition allegations regarding alleged Ayodhya donation embezzlement, asserting that the ongoing SIT probe would be unsparing and no one found complicit would be spared. This comes amidst a political storm where opposition parties, including SP and Congress, have criticized the BJP over financial discrepancies, while a BJP MP confirmed an FIR and eight arrests. Separately, a Ram Janmabhoomi Trust official expressed concern about innocent devotees being implicated, and a BJP MP dismissed calls for India-Pakistan dialogue until Pakistan ceases support for terrorism.
Content: New Delhi [India], July 2 (ANI): Responding to Akhilesh Yadav's allegations, Uttar Pradesh BJP President Pankaj Chaudhary on Wednesday dismissed the attacks as typical opposition politicking but warned that the ongoing Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe would be unsparing over the alleged Ayodhya donation embezzlement. Speaking to ANI, Chaudhary questioned Yadav's selective outrage, stating that the Chief Minister suggested discussions should also pivot to the land associated with Lord Krishna in Mathura. "The opposition's job is to raise questions, and Akhilesh Yadav has become particularly concerned about the Ram Mandir," Chaudhary remarked. "As for the Ram Mandir issue, whatever report the SIT submits and whatever findings emerge, no one will be spared." A fierce political storm has erupted over an alleged embezzlement case involving donations to the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya, drawing sharp rebukes from opposition leaders and triggering an aggressive defence from the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The controversy intensified after Samajwadi Party (SP) Chief Akhilesh Yadav levelled serious allegations against the management of the temple's funds, claiming that massive amounts of money from public donations have mysteriously gone missing. The allegations have rapidly united opposition forces, who are demanding absolute accountability over the sensitive issue. Backing the government's decisive action, BJP Rajya Sabha MP Manan Kumar Mishra revealed that a formal First Information Report (FIR) was immediately lodged and eight individuals have already been arrested as the scope of the investigation widens. "They have committed such a heinous crime and a grave sin. No punishment would be severe enough for such a despicable act," Mishra said, adding that merely resigning will not suffice for those found complicit. In Ayodhya, Prakash Gupta, the office in-charge of the Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust, expressed concern over the broad sweep of the ongoing SIT crackdown. While insisting that the truly guilty must be punished, Gupta cautioned that innocent, long-time devotees are getting caught in the crossfire. "My point is simple: the guilty must not go free, and no innocent person should be implicated. Some people are getting dragged into this who had absolutely no connection, yet the SIT is picking everyone up... I know some individuals used to work there selflessly, but you know how it is, if you get caught in the middle of it, you end up being labelled a thief too," said Prakash Gupta, Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust. Gupta added that due to the high-profile nature and inherent security concerns surrounding the suspects, subsequent court appearances and judicial hearings are increasingly being handled via video conferencing rather than physical transport. The opposition has used the opportunity to heavily criticise the ruling dispensation's religious politics. Congress Rajya Sabha MP Renuka Chowdhury accused the BJP of exploiting Lord Ram for electoral gains while overseeing financial discrepancies. "What they have done, we believe that. They built Ayodhya and lost... Now they are robbing lord Ram. They put Ram in the ballot box and reduced his Maryada Purushottam status. Now they are robbing him also. This is a bunch of thieves... Their people are sitting inside. What are they talking about? Now they want the SIT inquiry. Any child will tell you how much theft is happening," said Renuka Chowdhury, Congress RS MP. In Kerala, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) stated it would weaponise the issue locally to counter the BJP's narrative on temple management. CPI-M leader Thomas Isaac noted that Hindutva forces in Kerala constantly campaign that temples are unsafe under state government control. "The people who are saying temples are not secure with the government now will have to answer about how secure the temples are in the hands of the Hindutva forces," Isaac asserted. Amid separate developments regarding an open letter signed by over 100 citizens calling for restored India-Pakistan dialogue, BJP MP Manan Kumar Mishra heavily dismissed any immediate peace process. Mishra noted that India has no inherent issue with peace, but demanded that Pakistan first reform its habit of sheltering, training, and funding cross-border terrorists. Invoking recent military history, Mishra warned Islamabad against making threats. "And now Operation Sindoor happened just last year. Pakistan had to surrender within two days," Mishra highlighted. "Therefore, before any peace proposal, before any talks, Pakistan must control itself, reform itself, and stop its actions, its terrorist activities. Only then can any peace talks with India be held." (ANI) News agency subscription

Heading: Forgot Pahalgam? Congress leader furious at those demanding peace talks with Pakistan
Summary: Congress MP Manish Tewari has strongly criticized leaders, including Farooq Abdullah and Mehbooba Mufti, for signing an open letter advocating peace talks with Pakistan, citing Pakistan's history of terrorism and the Pahalgam Baisaran Valley massacre. Tewari questioned how these senior figures could forget past terrorist attacks that followed India's attempts at friendship. The BJP also condemned the letter, calling it an insult to martyrs and questioning its timing amidst India's aggressive anti-terrorism policy.
Content:
Congress MP Manish Tewari has openly criticized the leaders who signed an open letter to Prime Minister Modi and the Pakistani PM. He stated that peace talks cannot be advocated with a country that is intent on spreading terrorism in India.
Talks between India and Pakistan have been stalled since Operation Sindoor last year. An open letter has been written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Pakistani PM Shehbaz Sharif to restore diplomatic relations between India and Pakistan. This list of senior individuals includes prominent names like Farooq Abdullah, Mehbooba Mufti, and former RAW chief Dulat. While the BJP has reacted sharply to this list, senior Congress leader Manish Tewari has also criticized these individuals. Tewari questioned whether these people have forgotten the massacre in Pahalgam's Baisaran Valley so quickly?
Speaking to news agency ANI, Manish Tewari expressed his anger, saying it is unfortunate that these people have forgotten the Baisaran Valley massacre so quickly. They should understand that all attempts at dialogue with Pakistan so far have only been met with terrorism. Tewari said, "It is very unfortunate that some people have forgotten the massacre in Kashmir's Baisaran Valley. They have forgotten how innocent tourists and their families were brutally killed merely in the name of religion. Only one year, two months, and eight days have passed since this incident, yet some people are appealing for peace talks with Pakistan."
Tewari stated that history is witness that whenever India has tried to initiate talks with Pakistan, the response from the other side has always been through terrorism. He said, "Pakistan's strategy of promoting terrorism against India and weakening us by inflicting a thousand cuts is five decades old. In these five decades, every attempt by New Delhi to extend a hand of friendship has been followed by a terrorist attack. I am surprised how such senior people can forget history."
The Congress MP emphasized that one cannot imagine normalizing relations with a country that is bent on destroying India and spreading terror here. He said, "The vague emotional imagination of normalizing relations with Pakistan is completely beyond comprehension. God knows where the pressure is coming from, what invisible hand is pressuring people in India to normalize relations with Pakistan.
The entire matter is related to an open letter. More than 100 people from India and Pakistan, including former Jammu and Kashmir CM Farooq Abdullah, Mehbooba Mufti, and RJD MP Manoj Jha, have written an open letter to the Prime Ministers of both countries. It primarily emphasizes improving relations between the two countries, resuming diplomatic ties, restarting visa-related matters, and advancing talks on issues like Kashmir. However, after the letter came to light, the BJP has strongly criticized it.
BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla called the leaders who signed this letter an insult to martyrs. Questioning the timing of this letter, he said that this appeal from these leaders has come at a time when India is continuously adopting an aggressive policy against terrorism.

Heading: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit becomes the new Vice Chief of Air Staff
Summary: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit has been appointed as the new Vice Chief of Air Staff, receiving a Guard of Honour and paying respects at the National War Memorial. His significant contributions at the Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff include shaping integrated defence, conceptualizing military dialogues, and playing a key role in Defence Forces Vision 2047. A seasoned pilot commissioned in 1986, he has over 3,300 hours of flying experience across various aircraft.
Content:
Upon assuming the post of Vice Chief of Air Staff, Air Marshal Dixit was given a Guard of Honour at Vayu Bhawan. Before this ceremony, he visited the National War Memorial and paid floral tributes to the martyred heroes of the armed forces.

His tenure at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff is known for significant contributions that reshaped the nature of Integrated Defence. These include a key role in Operation Sindoor, conceptualizing military dialogue platforms like Ran Samvad 2025 and 2026, organizing Combined and Joint Commanders Conferences 2025 and 2026, and playing a crucial role in preparing the Defence Forces Vision 2047.

Air Marshal Dixit was commissioned into the fighter stream of the Indian Air Force in December 1986. He is a qualified Flying Instructor and Experimental Test Pilot with over 3,300 hours of experience flying more than 20 aircraft, including Mirage-2000, MiG-21, and Jaguar.
