Heading: Congress: Congress brings privilege motion against Rajnath
Summary: The Congress party has filed a privilege motion against Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, alleging he misled the Lok Sabha regarding casualties during "Operation Sindoor" in 2025. MP KC Venugopal stated that Rajnath had claimed no Indian soldiers were harmed, but the government later clarified that six soldiers were martyred. This discrepancy has become a new political issue, with the opposition expected to raise it during the upcoming Monsoon Session.
Content:
New Delhi: Congress today brought a privilege motion against Defense Minister Rajnath Singh. Congress has alleged that Rajnath misled the Lok Sabha by stating that no Indian soldier was martyred during Operation Sindoor in 2025, and MP KC Venugopal has brought a privilege motion against Rajnath for this. It is noteworthy that last week, after the central government clarified that 6 Indian soldiers were martyred during Operation Sindoor, the opposition has made this an issue.
They have alleged that the minister misled the House by giving false information in the Lok Sabha. Venugopal has also tagged the Lok Sabha proceedings in an application filed with the Speaker regarding this. Venugopal said that proceedings for breach of privilege against the minister should be initiated. In a letter to Birla, Venugopal stated that during the discussion in Parliament on July 28, 2025, regarding the Pahalgam terrorist attack and Operation Sindoor, Rajnath had said that no Indian soldier had suffered any harm.
But the government has now stated the exact opposite. The government has clarified that 6 Indian soldiers were martyred during Operation Sindoor. While Congress has now made this a new issue, there is strong speculation that opposition members may raise this issue and create a ruckus in the upcoming Monsoon Session.

Heading: Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar takes command of Southern Command
Summary: Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar has assumed command as the GOC-in-C of the Indian Army's Southern Command, succeeding Lt Gen Sandeep Jain. With over four decades of distinguished service, including various command, staff, and international roles, he has been honored with several prestigious military awards. Upon taking charge, he paid tribute to martyrs and emphasized maintaining operational readiness, enhancing joint efficiency, indigenous capacity development, and integrating emerging technologies for national service.
Content:
Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar, AVSM, VSM, assumed charge as the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief (GOC-in-C) of the Southern Command of the Indian Army on July 1, 2026. He succeeded Lieutenant General Sandeep Jain, AVSM, SM, who recently took over as the Vice Chief of the Army Staff.

More than four decades of military experience

An alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar was commissioned into the 74 Armoured Regiment in December 1988. He has had a glorious military career spanning over four decades, during which he has held several important command, staff, and training responsibilities in various geographical and operational conditions. As the General Officer Commanding of the II Corps during Operation Sindoor, he demonstrated decisive leadership and strategic foresight.

Led many important commands

Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar has commanded an armoured regiment in an operational area, a strategic independent armoured brigade, an infantry division, and a major strike corps in the Western Sector. He has also served in important positions such as Colonel Military Secretary in a Strike Corps, Colonel General Staff of an Armoured Division in the Western Sector, Brigadier Quartermaster General of a Strike Corps, Brigadier General Staff of an Operational Command, Additional Director General (Armoured Corps), and Director General Territorial Army. He has also served as an instructor at the National Defence Academy, Khadakwasla.

Also held international responsibilities

The General Officer has also served as a member of the Indian Military Training Team in Bhutan and as Defence and Military Attaché in the Indian Embassies in Armenia and Belarus. In addition to graduating from the National Defence Academy, he has pursued higher education from the Defence Services Staff College, College of Defence Management, and National Defence College of India. He holds postgraduate degrees in Defence and Strategic Studies, Management Studies, and Defence and International Relations.

Honored with several prestigious military awards

Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar has been honored with the Ati Vishisht Seva Medal (AVSM), Vishisht Seva Medal (VSM), Chief of Army Staff Commendation, and three Army Commanders' Commendations for his distinguished services.

Pai d tribute to brave martyrs

After assuming charge, Lieutenant General Rajesh Pushkar paid tribute to the brave martyrs at the Southern Command War Memorial and inspected the Guard of Honour at the Southern Command Headquarters. He reiterated his commitment to maintaining the highest operational readiness of the Southern Command, emphasizing enhancing joint efficiency, indigenous capacity development, and rapid integration of emerging technologies. He expressed confidence that all officers and jawans would uphold the glorious traditions of the Indian Army and maintain the highest operational excellence in the service of the nation.

Heading: RSS leader Ram Madhav's secret meeting with Pakistan officials: Hariprasad's accusation
Summary: KPCC President B. K. Hariprasad accused RSS leader Ram Madhav of holding four secret meetings with Pakistani officials, including a former ISI Major General, in Colombo and London. Hariprasad criticized the BJP for assigning Madhav election responsibilities, questioning his authority to engage in foreign policy discussions and alleging a cover-up regarding soldier casualties in 'Operation Sindoor'. He challenged Madhav to answer these questions, accusing the BJP of diverting election discourse with divisive topics.
Content: Bengaluru: KPCC President B. K. Hariprasad has alleged that Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) leader Ram Madhav held four secret meetings with Pakistani officials. Speaking at a seminar of the publicity committee held at Bharat Jodo Bhavan, he shared a snippet of his speech on social media platform X. During this, he criticized the BJP for entrusting RSS leader Ram Madhav with the responsibility of the Greater Bengaluru Development Authority (GBA) election. 'You should look at Ram Madhav's history. He held 4 meetings in Colombo, London, and a secret meeting with a former Major General of Pakistan's ISI. Recently, his guru Mohan Bhagwat said there is nothing wrong with talking to Pakistan. When I spoke similarly, they hounded me for 2 years. They left my company after going to Pakistan and eating biryani,' he lashed out. 'They had said that none of our soldiers died in Operation Sindoor. But just recently, Rajnath Singh offered condolences, stating that 6 soldiers died. This shows how many lies they tell. They cannot even name those who sacrificed their lives for the country. Operation Sindoor took place 2 months ago, and Ram Madhav held a meeting in London then. When our government was at the center, it clearly stated that there would be no talks with Pakistan until terrorism was suppressed,' he informed. Hariprasad, who said, 'When elections come, BJP talks about Pakistan, chicken, mutton, halal, hijab, mangalsutra,' challenged, 'Ram Madhav must answer some of my questions when he comes for the GBA election.' 'Who gave him the authority to hold secret meetings with Pakistanis? He is neither a foreign minister, nor an MLA, nor an MP. Who gave an RSS Pracharak the authority to hold meetings abroad? What authority do RSS members have to decide on foreign policy? Why was the country's public not informed about the secret meeting with Pakistanis? Why were the names of Indian soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor kept hidden for so long? We need to ask such questions. We need to awaken the people,' he said.

Heading: Same as Original
Summary: General Dhiraj Seth, the new Indian Army Chief, has introduced the 'Vijay' mantra to prepare the army for future challenges. This acronym, standing for Vigilance, Innovation, Jointness, Aatmanirbharta (self-sufficiency), and 'Yoddha First', outlines his focus on building a technology-enabled, self-reliant force. The initiative aims to enhance operational readiness, leverage indigenous capabilities, and foster synergy across military branches to adapt to evolving modern warfare.
Content:
A day after taking over as the Chief of the Army Staff, General Dhiraj Seth has outlined the ‘Vijay’ mantra to make the Indian Army future-ready.
General Dhiraj Seth on Wednesday outlined the ‘Vijay’ mantra to make the Indian Army future-ready.
A day after taking over as the Chief of the Army Staff, Seth said that his objective would be build the Indian Army as a technology-enabled, future-ready force.
Seth summed up his focus areas in the acronym ‘Vijay’, which means victory in Hindi. He explained what Vijay stood for: V for vigilance and readiness, I for innovation and transformation, J for jointness and integration, A for aatmanirbharta (self-sufficiency), and Y for ‘Yoddha First’ (Soldier First).
Seth said that these focus areas are a result of guidance provided by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh under the ‘Decade of Transformation’ initiative.
Seth took over as the 31st Indian Army chief on Tuesday after General Upendra Dwivedi’s retirement. As a three-star general, he commanded South Western Command and Southern Command — a rare feat of commanding two operational commands. He also commanded the Bhopal-headquartered 21 Corps, a strike formation that is tasked with offensive thrusts into Pakistan during wartime.
#WATCH | Delhi: Army Chief Gen Dhiraj Seth says, "...To tackle the challenges of this evolving security environment, we must advance the modernisation of the Army with renewed vigour and firm resolve. Our objective is to build a technology-enabled, future-ready Army that is… pic.twitter.com/R3rh5yQC3p
Seth went on to elaborate his five focus areas summed up in the ‘Vijay’ mantra:
‘V’ for Vigilance : “We will maintain constant vigilance regarding our borders and emerging threats, and uphold a high level of operational readiness to effectively counter any challenge to national security.”
‘I’ for Innovation : “‘I’ stands for Innovation and Transformation. My focus will be on both doctrinal and technological solutions. Innovation will be an integral part of our mindset, operational methods, and capability development. Furthermore, we will implement the transformations necessary to adapt to the evolving battlefield.”
‘J’ for Jointness : “To enhance the Indian Army’s operational effectiveness, we will maintain synergy, complete coordination and alignment with the Air Force and the Navy. This integrated approach will enable us to participate in nation-building and propel us towards the goal of a ‘Viksit Bharat 2047’.”
‘A’ stands for Aatmanirbharta : “Leveraging indigenous capabilities and technologies developed within the country, we will build a self-reliant Army. Our overarching aim will be to win wars using indigenous solutions.”
‘Y’ stands for ‘Yoddha First’ : “In my definition, everyone from the newest Agniveer to the most senior veteran is a warrior, and these warriors constitute the greatest strength of our Army.”
Seth has taken charge at a time when the Indian Army, along with the other military branches, are in the midst of transformation as they face a fast-evolving battlefield. The rapid advance of drone technology in recent years, mainstreaming of drones, rising importance of digital capabilities, and emergence of space as both an active theatre and force-multiplier has changed the nature of modern warfare.
Last year’s Operation Sindoor was India’s first experience with sustained combat in this new age of modern warfare. Analysts have noted that lessons from the four-day conflict, including the prominent usage of drones, are guiding the military’s modernisation and reforms.

Heading: KPCC chief questions Ram Madhav's alleged Pakistan meetings
Summary: KPCC President BK Hariprasad questioned the authority under which senior RSS leader Ram Madhav allegedly held meetings with Pakistani representatives abroad, demanding clarification from the Union government. Hariprasad also criticized the Centre's statements on 'Operation Sindoor' and accused the BJP of using emotive issues during elections instead of addressing governance. He further launched an ideological attack on the BJP and RSS, contrasting their alleged actions with India's constitutional values and crediting past Congress governments for national development.
Content: Bengaluru, July 1 (UNI) Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) President BK Hariprasad on Wednesday questioned the authority under which senior Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh leader Ram Madhav allegedly held meetings with Pakistani representatives, asking who had empowered an RSS functionary to engage in matters concerning India's foreign policy. Addressing a seminar at Bharat Jodo Bhavan here, Hariprasad alleged that Ram Madhav had convened meetings in Colombo and London, including what he described as a "secret meeting" with a former Major General of Pakistan's Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI). He demanded that the union government explain under whose authorisation such engagements had taken place. "Ram Madhav is neither the External Affairs Minister nor a Member of Parliament or a legislator. Who authorised an RSS pracharak to hold discussions with Pakistani representatives abroad? On what authority are RSS leaders taking decisions or engaging in discussions on India's foreign policy?" Hariprasad asked. He further questioned why the alleged meetings had not been disclosed to the public and urged the BJP to clarify the purpose and outcome of the interactions. Linking the issue to national security, Hariprasad also alleged inconsistencies in the Centre's statements regarding "Operation Sindoor". He claimed the government had initially maintained that no Indian soldiers were killed during the operation, but later Defence Minister Rajnath Singh paid tribute to six personnel who lost their lives. "If soldiers sacrificed their lives for the nation, why were their names withheld for so long? The country deserves transparency," he said, while alleging that the BJP government had made contradictory statements on the issue. The KPCC chief accused the Bharatiya Janata Party of invoking Pakistan and other emotive issues such as hijab, halal, chicken, mutton and mangalsutra during elections instead of addressing governance and public welfare. Hariprasad said these questions should be placed before the people ahead of the forthcoming Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) elections and urged Congress workers to expose what he termed the BJP's "double standards" on nationalism. Launching a broader ideological attack on the BJP and the RSS, he said India's democracy was built on the sacrifices of freedom fighters and the values enshrined in the Constitution. He alleged that organisations which opposed the freedom movement continued to work against the country's founding principles. "The RSS and BJP will not face opposition from us if they accept the Constitution, the national tricolour and Mahatma Gandhi's philosophy of communal harmony. They are fellow Indians, but they must accept the values on which the Republic stands," he said. Hariprasad credited successive Congress governments led by former Prime Ministers Jawaharlal Nehru and Indira Gandhi with transforming India from a food-deficit nation into one of the world's largest producers of foodgrains and milk through the Green Revolution and other developmental initiatives. He accused the BJP of attempting to erode India's pluralistic character through policies promoting "one nation, one education, one leader and one religion", asserting that the country's diversity remained its greatest strength. Hariprasad also appealed to Congress leaders and workers to focus on publicising the achievements and welfare initiatives of the Karnataka government while preparing for the upcoming civic elections in Bengaluru. KPCC Campaign Committee Chairman Vinay Kumar Sorake, former minister Rani Satish, Kimmane Rathnakar, Shivanna, former MP L Hanumanthaiah and several party leaders attended the seminar. UNI BDN

Heading: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit Assumes Charge as New Deputy Chief of Air Staff
Summary: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit has taken over as the new Deputy Chief of Air Staff, succeeding Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor. Dixit, a veteran with over 3,300 hours of flying experience across 20 aircraft types, was previously the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff. He was honored with a Guard of Honour and paid respects at the National War Memorial upon assuming his new role.
Content:
New Delhi - Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who previously served as 'Chief of Integrated Defence Staff' during 'Operation Sindoor', assumed charge as the new Deputy Chief of Air Staff on Wednesday. He replaced Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor, who retired on June 30 after serving four decades in the Indian Air Force. Air Marshal Dixit was accorded a 'Guard of Honour' at 'Vayu Bhawan', the Air Force Headquarters, upon assuming the charge as the new Deputy Chief of Air Staff.
Before the ceremony, Dixit visited the National War Memorial and paid tribute to the martyrs of the armed forces by laying a wreath. Prior to being appointed Deputy Chief, he served as the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff (CISC) at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) here. Air Marshal Dixit assumed the post of CISC on May 1, 2025, a position he held until June 30.
Air Marshal Dixit joined the fighter branch of the Indian Air Force in December 1986. He is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy at Khadakwasla, the 'Defence Services Staff' College in Bangladesh, and the National Defence College in New Delhi. The Ministry of Defence had earlier stated that Air Marshal Dixit is a "skilled flight instructor and test pilot with over 3,300 hours of experience flying 20 types of aircraft, including Mirage-2000, MiG-21, and Jaguar." According to officials, Air Marshal Tejinder Singh will assume charge as the next CISC.

Heading: Complaint of misleading Parliament; Privilege motion against Union BJP Minister: Congress senior leader's letter to Speaker
Summary: Senior Congress leader K.C. Venugopal has sought privilege action against Union Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, alleging he misled Parliament by stating no Indian soldiers died during 'Operation Sindoor' in 2025, despite later revelations of six casualties. Venugopal criticized the government for allegedly lying about soldiers' sacrifices, calling it an insult to their families and the armed forces. The Ministry of Defense, however, clarified that the minister's statement was taken out of context and false information was being spread.
Content:
New Delhi: Senior Congress leader K.C. Venugopal has submitted a letter to the Speaker seeking privilege action against Defense Minister Rajnath Singh for providing false information in Parliament. Following the Pahalgam terrorist attack on April 22, 2025, which killed 26 people, the Indian Army launched a military operation called 'Operation Sindoor'. During a debate in Parliament on July 28, 2025, regarding this incident, Union Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, a senior BJP leader, stated that no Indian soldiers were harmed.

However, it was recently revealed that 6 armed forces personnel, including 5 from the Indian Army and one from the Air Force, died in 'Operation Sindoor', and their names are inscribed on the National War Memorial. In this context, K.C. Venugopal, a senior leader of the Congress party and chairman of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament, wrote a letter to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla yesterday. In his letter, submitted under Lok Sabha Rule 223, he emphasized, "The Defense Minister's statement in Parliament that there were no casualties during 'Operation Sindoor' is completely false and an act of misleading Parliament. Considering that misleading Parliament and concealing information constitute a breach of privilege and contempt of Parliament, privilege action should be taken against the Defense Minister."

Furthermore, in a post he published on the X platform, he criticized, "How is it possible for the forces to announce a year later that we lost 6 soldiers, after stating in July 2025 that no Indian soldier was martyred? This information is a great insult to the families of the 6 soldiers who sacrificed their lives in the service of protecting the nation, and to the entire armed forces. The Union government has lied about the sacrifice of the soldiers." In response, the Ministry of Defense issued a clarification stating, "Only a part of the Defense Minister's speech in Parliament on July 28 last year is being isolated, and deliberately false information is being spread on social media claiming that he stated no Indian soldier died in 'Operation Sindoor'."

Heading: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit takes charge as new Vice Chief of Air Staff
Summary: Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit has assumed the role of new Vice Chief of Air Staff, succeeding Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor. Previously, he served as the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff, where he was instrumental in 'Operation Sindoor' and advanced integrated defense strategies, including the 'Defence Force Vision-2047'. Dixit, a highly experienced pilot, received a Guard of Honour and paid respects at the National War Memorial upon his appointment.
Content:
New Delhi, July 1 (भाषा) Air Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, who served as the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff during 'Operation Sindoor', took charge as the new Vice Chief of Air Staff on Wednesday.
He replaced Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor, who retired on June 30 after four decades of service in the Indian Air Force.
Air Marshal Dixit was given a 'Guard of Honour' at Air Force Headquarters 'Vayu Bhawan' on taking charge as the new Vice Chief of Air Staff. Before the ceremony, Dixit paid tribute to the martyred soldiers of the armed forces by laying a wreath at the National War Memorial.
Before being appointed as Vice Chief, he was serving as the Chief of Integrated Defence Staff (CISC) at Headquarters Integrated Defence Staff (HQ IDS) here.
Air Marshal Dixit had assumed the charge of CISC on May 1, 2025, a position he held till June 30.
HQ IDS said in a post on social media platform 'X' on Tuesday, "During his tenure at this headquarters, several important steps were taken to give a new direction to the integrated defense system. He played a significant role in 'Operation Sindoor', which proved to be a decisive campaign from the perspective of India's national security."
It said, "Under his leadership, 20 joint principles and reference manuals institutionalizing the views of the three services were released. He conceptualized unprecedented military dialogue initiatives like 'Ran Samvad-2025' and 'Ran Samvad-2026', successfully coordinated joint commander conferences in 2025 and 2026, and played a key role in preparing the draft of 'Defence Force Vision-2047' - a transformative document outlining a technology-based, integrated and future-ready armed forces."
The armed forces carried out 'Operation Sindoor' in May 2025 in response to the Pahalgam terrorist attack. Military officials and experts have often emphasized the integration that the three services demonstrated during this military operation.
Air Marshal Dixit joined the 'fighter branch' of the Indian Air Force in December 1986. He is an alumnus of the National Defence Academy, Khadakwasla, Defence Services Staff College, Bangladesh, and National Defence College, New Delhi.
The Ministry of Defence had earlier stated that Air Marshal Dixit is a 'skilled flight instructor and test pilot, with over 3,300 hours of experience flying more than 20 types of aircraft including Mirage-2000, MiG-21 and Jaguar.'
According to officials, Air Marshal Tejinder Singh will take over as the next CISC.

Heading: 'Misled Lok Sabha': Congress Moves Privilege Notice Against Rajnath Singh Over Operation Sindoor Remark
Summary: Congress leader KC Venugopal has moved a breach of privilege notice against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of misleading the Lok Sabha regarding casualties in Operation Sindoor. Venugopal claims Singh falsely stated no soldiers were killed, a statement contradicted by the official acknowledgement of six fatalities whose names are now inscribed at the National War Memorial. The Congress leader asserts this constitutes a "clear-cut lie" and dishonors the martyrs, demanding privilege proceedings against the Minister.
Content:
Venugopal cited the official acknowledgement of six Operation Sindoor fatalities, claiming it contradicted Rajnath Singh's statement in Parliament and warranted privilege action.
Congress leader KC Venugopal on Tuesday sought breach of privilege proceedings against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of misleading the Lok Sabha over the deaths of Indian armed forces personnel during Operation Sindoor.
Venugopal wrote to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, alleging that Singh’s statement in Parliament during the July 2025 debate on Operation Sindoor, that no Indian soldier had been killed during the operation, was contradicted by the subsequent official acknowledgement that six security personnel had laid down their lives.
Sharing details of his letter on X, Venugopal accused the Defence Minister of making what he described as a “straightforward, clear-cut lie" before the House.
“In the debate in the Lok Sabha on Operation Sindoor, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh lied to the people of India. It was a straightforward, clear-cut lie – to mislead the House. How could he, in July 2025, say that no Indian soldier was martyred, and then a year later the forces announce that we have lost 6 jawans?" Venugopal mentioned in his post.
The Congress general secretary further alleged that the government’s handling of the issue had dishonoured the sacrifice of the soldiers who died during the operation.
“It is a grave insult to the families of these six martyrs and the entire armed forces that the people of India were not told of their bravery and ultimate sacrifice," he said.
He also asserted that the soldiers lost their lives while protecting the country from its enemies, but claimed that “the so-called nationalist Government simply lied about their martyrdom."
Venugopal said he had requested the Lok Sabha Speaker to initiate privilege proceedings against the Defence Minister, arguing that misleading Parliament or withholding information from the House amounts to a breach of privilege and contempt of the House.
In his post, the Congress leader also shared a copy of the breach of privilege notice submitted against Rajnath Singh.
Referring to the Defence Minister’s earlier statement in Parliament, the notice stated that official records now acknowledge the deaths of six armed forces personnel during Operation Sindoor.
The notice named them as Subedar Major Pawan Kumar of the Indian Army, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Vir Chakra, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Aviation Technician Mood Murlinaik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh, all from the Indian Army, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar, Vayu Sena Medal, of the Indian Air Force.
“The aforementioned position clearly indicates that the Minister of Defence, while stating on the floor of the House that there had been no casualties during Operation Sindoor, was clearly misleading and incorrect," the notice said.
“It is well established that misleading the House or withholding information from the House by a Minister on the Floor of the House constitutes a breach of privilege and contempt of the House. In view of the foregoing, I request that privilege proceedings may be initiated against the Minister of Defence in the matter," it added.
The development comes after the names of the six Indian security personnel who lost their lives during Operation Sindoor in May 2025 were inscribed at the National War Memorial in New Delhi.
Operation Sindoor was launched by India in response to the terror attack in Pahalgam, targeting terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK). India later carried out strikes on Pakistani airbases after Islamabad escalated the conflict, according to official accounts.
The government has not yet issued a response to the allegations made by the Congress leader or the privilege notice submitted before the Lok Sabha Speaker.

Heading: PIOs or Muslims—who is Modi govt aiming at when it says passport isn’t citizenship proof?
Summary: The article examines the Indian government's assertion that a passport is not proof of citizenship, highlighting the confusion and potential implications of this stance. The author speculates on the government's motives, suggesting it could either be to accommodate Persons of Indian Origin or, more concerningly, to disenfranchise certain communities, particularly Muslims, through the controversial SIR process. It concludes by calling for the Supreme Court to intervene and clarify the definition of Indian citizenship, warning against the fragility of this concept.
Content:
T wo developments only days apart have shed light on how the controversy over citizenship has become an integral part of the already dubious SIR process.

The first was a seemingly casual remark by a senior official of the Minister of External Affairs that the Indian passport is not a proof of citizenship, but only a travel document. In purely technical terms, the official was right. Passports and citizenship are governed by different Acts. It is legitimate to argue that the two should not be conflated.

Nor is this a new debate. Way back in the 1980s, a corporate war led the government to issue a deportation notice to a businessman who held a British passport. The businessman challenged the order, arguing that his British passport was merely a travel document and that he continued to be an Indian citizen.

The courts appeared to accept the argument. The deportation did not go ahead. But, just to avoid any further attacks from politicians who favoured his rivals, the businessman said he would apply for an Indian passport as well.

And yet the confusion continues. For instance, every time the law requires a person to be an Indian citizen, the government does not take the line that anyone with a foreign passport could still be an Indian citizen because the two concepts — passports and citizenship — are different. Newspaper editors were required to be Indian citizens and the official way to ascertain that was by checking their passports. Nobody said, ‘so what if he has a Brazilian passport. He might still be an Indian citizen.’



As far as officialdom is concerned, you are not an Indian citizen unless you have an Indian passport. That position has now been modified to suit the government: even if you do have an Indian passport, you may still be regarded as not being an Indian citizen.

Yes, there is a technical issue here: the two separate Acts. But there is also a reality. Nobody who goes to a passport office and demands a passport will be issued one unless the authorities are convinced that he or she is an Indian citizen. If you say, ‘I am a Brazilian but want an Indian passport,’ they will

throw you out of the passport office.

So, why does the government think that the distinction is worth emphasising? At first, I thought the MEA official was making a casual remark about the technical position, but given that the government has not rushed to reassure citizens or clarify the matter, I am no longer sure what its motives are.

Is it, as some have suggested, preparing the ground for giving Indian passports to American citizens of Indian origin? Many have been demanding something like this for years. Certainly, such a move would appeal to the BJP’s PIO support base: people who sit in, say New Jersey, and tell us how India should be run but when it comes to the crunch, when we expect them to lobby American legislators on India’s behalf (as we did during Operation Sindoor), they say “Sorry pal, I am an American citizen; it’s not my problem.”

I am sure many of them would gladly accept Indian passports while hanging on to their US citizenship. Once you say that passports and citizenship are unrelated, this becomes possible to implement.

Or is the intention more negative?

Over the past few years, there has been a conscious attempt to redefine who an Indian is. Is this casual remark part of that exercise? Now that the technical distinction between passport holders and citizens has been re-emphasised, it will become more difficult for lakhs of people to prove that they are Indians. It is no secret whose Indianness is under suspicion: Muslims, mainly.

Whatever you think of the motives behind this move, no reasonable person can deny that the SIR process has disenfranchised members of the Muslim minority. It is true that the BJP would have won West Bengal anyway, but the voting figures clearly demonstrate that in many constituencies the BJP’s majority swelled because Muslim voters had been struck off the rolls.



Which brings us to the second worrying development of the last week. A well known anti-BJP former editor has said that his passport was not renewed and he was unable to go abroad for his daughter’s wedding. As far as we can tell, the problem was that the police verification was denied. And why was it denied?

Well, because he was not on the post-SIR electoral rolls. As he used to edit one of Kolkata’s most famous newspapers, The Telegraph , and is not what the BJP would call a termite or an infiltrator (and while it should not matter but may be worth mentioning that he is a Hindu), it seems strange to remove him from the electoral rolls. It is even stranger that getting a passport renewal now depends on how a citizen fared in the notoriously dodgy and controversial SIR exercise.

It is entirely possible that the two phenomena — the citizenship controversy and the use of SIR-fiddled rolls to renew a passport — are not connected and that the timing is co-incidental.

Either way, it shows us how fragile the concept of citizenship is becoming in our country.

The Supreme Court has taken a largely passive attitude to the SIR issue. In retrospect, that may have been a mistake. It’s no longer just the possibility of rigging an election that the judiciary has to consider. Now that this flawed and probably malign SIR exercise is being used to deny our very Indianness and our rights as citizens, it may be time for the Supreme Court to take a less passive role and clarify what it means to be an Indian.

It owes that much to posterity. What binds us is our Indianness. Take that away and you signal the beginning of a national collapse.

Vir Sanghvi is a print and television journalist and talk show host. He tweets @virsanghvi.

Heading: Letter written to PM Modi and Shehbaz Sharif, BJP furious at these Indians; Which leaders are involved?
Summary: Over 100 Indian and Pakistani leaders, including Farooq Abdullah and Mehbooba Mufti, have written an open letter to PM Modi and Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif, urging them to resume dialogue for peace in South Asia. The ruling BJP has strongly condemned this appeal, labeling the signatories as "terror supporters" and questioning their timing, especially after recent terror attacks. BJP spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla emphasized India's firm stance against terrorism and accused the leaders of insulting the armed forces by advocating talks with Pakistan.
Content:
More than 100 leaders, including Farooq Abdullah, Mehbooba Mufti, and former RAW chief, have appealed to PM Modi to start talks with Pakistan, a move that has drawn a sharp retort from the BJP, calling them 'terror supporters'.
A new political controversy has erupted over the demand to restore peace and diplomatic relations between India and Pakistan. National Conference president Farooq Abdullah, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, and RJD MP Manoj Jha, along with over 100 Indian and Pakistani leaders and civil society members, have written an open letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Pakistan's PM Shehbaz Sharif.
However, as soon as this letter came to light, the ruling BJP reacted sharply, labeling these leaders as 'terror supporters'. The appeal was coordinated by O.P. Shah, head of the New Delhi-based think tank 'Center for Peace and Progress'. The letter urges the Prime Ministers of both countries to take meaningful steps for the restoration of peace, dialogue, and cooperation in South Asia.
The letter advocates for several important steps to improve relations between the two countries.
From India, Farooq Abdullah, Mehbooba Mufti, Manoj Jha, separatist leader Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, former RAW chief A.S. Dulat, Mani Shankar Aiyar, Humayun Kabir, Jawhar Sircar, Mohammad Yusuf Tarigami, Prof. Saifuddin Soz, and Prof. Apoorvanand, among others, have signed it.
From Pakistan, former Foreign Minister Khurshid Mahmud Kasuri, former Ambassador Ashraf Jehangir Qazi, academic Pervez Hoodbhoy, former Senator Farhatullah Babar, Beena Sarwar, Salima Hashmi, and A.H. Nayyar, among others, have signed. Here are the 61 Indians who signed the letter-
Separatist leader Mirwaiz Umar Farooq defended this appeal. He said that if America and Iran can return to the negotiating table after conflict, then India and Pakistan should also engage in dialogue. He argued that wars do not resolve disputes; only dialogue can resolve long-standing issues, including Kashmir.
Following this move, the BJP launched a scathing attack on the signatories. BJP national spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla called these leaders 'supporters of terror' and questioned their timing. Poonawalla stated that this appeal comes at a time when India is adopting a very strict policy against terrorism after the 'Pahalgam terror attack'.
Referring to 'Operation Sindoor', he said that India has made it clear that it will not differentiate between terrorists and those who harbor them. Poonawalla recalled India's decision to suspend the Indus Water Treaty, stating that 'New India' gives a befitting reply to terrorism. He alleged that instead of standing with the army and victims of terror, these leaders are repeatedly advocating for talks with Pakistan. The BJP spokesperson sarcastically remarked, "These are the same people who questioned the surgical strike, Balakot airstrike, and Operation Sindoor. This new move of theirs is a direct insult to the martyrs and armed forces of the country."

Heading: 'Parliament misled on Operation Sindoor', Privilege notice against Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, Congress-BJP clash
Summary: A political controversy has erupted over Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's statement on 'Operation Sindoor,' with Congress accusing him of misleading Parliament regarding military casualties. Congress claims the minister initially stated no soldiers were martyred, while later official data confirmed six casualties, prompting a demand for privilege proceedings. The Defense Ministry, however, refutes these allegations, asserting that the minister's statement was taken out of context.
Content:
The political controversy over Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's statement regarding Operation Sindoor has intensified. The Congress has accused him of misleading Parliament and has demanded Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla initiate privilege proceedings against him. Congress states that the Defense Minister had initially said that no Indian soldier was martyred during the operation, while later official information confirmed the martyrdom of six military personnel. Meanwhile, the Ministry of Defense has called these allegations misleading, stating that the minister's statement was presented out of context.

**Demand for Privilege Notice against Rajnath Singh**

Congress MP and General Secretary (Organization) K.C. Venugopal has written a letter to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, demanding the initiation of privilege proceedings against Defense Minister Rajnath Singh. K.C. Venugopal said that during the discussion on Operation Sindoor in the Lok Sabha, the Defense Minister lied to the people of the country and the House. He alleged that 'this was a clear and direct lie that misled Parliament.'

**Questions raised on 'No Casualty' statement**

Congress says that in July 2025, the Defense Minister had stated that no Indian soldier was martyred during Operation Sindoor. But a year later, the Indian Armed Forces themselves revealed that a total of six military personnel, including five army soldiers and one air force personnel, were martyred in this operation. K.C. Venugopal said that it is a serious insult to the families of these six martyrs and the entire Indian Armed Forces that the people of the country were not informed about their bravery and supreme sacrifice.

**Letter written to Lok Sabha Speaker**

The Congress leader has demanded action for breach of privilege against the Defense Minister in a letter written to the Lok Sabha Speaker. K.C. Venugopal, MP from Alappuzha, Kerala, has given a privilege notice under Rule 223 of the Lok Sabha. In his letter, he has referred to the discussion held in the Lok Sabha on July 28, 2025, regarding the Pahalgam terrorist attack and Operation Sindoor. The letter states that the Defense Minister had said in the House that no Indian soldier was martyred while performing duty during Operation Sindoor.

**Citing official statement**

K.C. Venugopal said that recently released official statements have revealed information about the martyrdom of five Indian Army personnel and one Air Force personnel. He said that this clearly shows that the statement given in the Lok Sabha was misleading and factually incorrect. The Congress leader said that misleading the House or concealing information is considered a breach of parliamentary privilege and contempt of the House. He requested the Lok Sabha Speaker to initiate action in this matter.

**Names of six martyrs added to War Memorial**

This demand comes at a time when the names of six military personnel martyred during Operation Sindoor were recently inscribed at the National War Memorial in New Delhi. The government publicly revealed the identities of these martyred soldiers for the first time.

**Defense Ministry calls claims misleading**

After the controversy escalated, the Ministry of Defense called the claims circulating on social media misleading. The ministry said that a part of the Defense Minister's speech was presented out of context. According to the Ministry of Defense, Rajnath Singh had not said that no soldier was martyred in Operation Sindoor. The ministry states that his statement was a response to the false claim that Indian Air Force pilots were killed.

Heading: Can India, Pakistan Turn The Page? 100+ Citizens From Both Nations Write To PM Modi, Shehbaz Sharif
Summary: Over 100 prominent citizens from India and Pakistan have appealed to Prime Ministers Modi and Sharif to restore peace, dialogue, and normal relations, including full diplomatic ties, visa services, and structured bilateral discussions on all outstanding issues. They also called for reopening trade routes, bus services, airspace, and religious corridors. However, the BJP strongly criticized the signatories, labeling them "terror apologists" and questioning their timing given India's tough stance against terrorism, citing actions like Operation Sindoor and surgical strikes.
Content:
From India, the signatories included Farooq Abdullah, separatist leader Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, RJD MP Manoj Jha and AJUP leader Humayun Kabir.
A year after Operation Sindoor, more than 100 prominent citizens from India and Pakistan have appealed to Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his Pakistani counterpart, Shehbaz Sharif, to take meaningful and sustained steps towards restoring peace, dialogue and normal relations between the two countries.
The appeal, issued by the Centre for Peace and Progress, was signed by 117 people from both sides of the border. The signatories urged the two governments to end the continued hostility, saying it was depriving millions of young people of opportunities, prosperity and a secure future.
Among the key demands were the restoration of full diplomatic relations, the reinstatement of High Commissioners in New Delhi and Islamabad, and the resumption of normal visa services for citizens of both countries.
The letter was signed by 61 prominent figures from India and 56 from Pakistan.
From India, the signatories included National Conference chief Farooq Abdullah, separatist leader Mirwaiz Umar Farooq, PDP chief Mehbooba Mufti, RJD MP Manoj Jha and AJUP leader Humayun Kabir.
On the Pakistan side, the signatories included former Foreign Minister Khurshid Mahmud Kasuri, diplomat Ashraf Jehangir Qazi, National Assembly member Isphanyar Bhandara and nuclear physicist and author Pervez Hoodbhoy.
The letter said India and Pakistan together are home to nearly one-fifth of the world’s population, with a large share comprising young people. “The people of both countries deserve a future defined by peace, development, connectivity and cooperation, rather than perpetual mistrust and confrontation," the letter stated.
It added that decades of estrangement had limited the collective potential of both countries while imposing significant social, economic and human costs.
According to the signatories, sustained engagement and dialogue remain the only viable way to resolve differences and build a stable and prosperous region.
The group urged the two Prime Ministers to restore full diplomatic relations, appoint High Commissioners in New Delhi and Islamabad, and resume regular visa services.
The signatories also called for the reopening of a structured bilateral dialogue covering all outstanding issues. These included discussions on Jammu and Kashmir, revisiting the framework negotiated between 2004 and 2007, taking steps towards demilitarisation and de-escalation, while addressing the legitimate security concerns of both countries.
The letter further proposed reopening the Attari-Wagah land border for trade and travel and restoring the Srinagar-Muzaffarabad bus service along with other connectivity initiatives.
It also sought the reopening of airspace for commercial airlines to reduce travel time and costs and improve connectivity between the two countries.
The signatories urged both governments to reopen the Kartarpur Sahib Corridor as a confidence-building measure. They also called for opening Sharada Peeth, the sacred religious site of Kashmiri Pandits located in Pakistan’s Neelum Valley, and facilitating visits to religious and cultural heritage sites on both sides of the border.
Appealing directly to the two Prime Ministers, the letter urged them to respond to the aspirations of ordinary citizens.
“We respectfully request you to listen to the aspirations of common people and choose engagement over isolation, dialogue over hostility and cooperation over confrontation. The future of South Asia should be shaped not by division and conflict, but by peace, prosperity and shared progress," it said.
The signatories also clarified that the appeal was not intended to endorse any political position but was aimed at placing the welfare and future of nearly two billion people above conflict and division. They said peace, dialogue and cooperation remain the surest path towards a stable, prosperous and secure South Asia.
The BJP strongly criticised the signatories, accusing them of acting as “terror apologists" by repeatedly calling for dialogue with Pakistan despite its continued support for cross-border terrorism. BJP national spokesperson Shehzad Poonawalla said the appeal came at a time when India had adopted a tougher stance against terrorism following the Pahalgam terror attack.
Referring to Operation Sindoor, he said India no longer distinguishes between terrorists and those who shelter them. Poonawalla also cited the suspension of the Indus Waters Treaty, alleging that the signatories had earlier questioned the surgical strikes, the Balakot airstrikes and Operation Sindoor, calling their latest appeal an insult to India’s armed forces and martyrs.

Summary: Congress leader KC Venugopal has moved a privilege notice against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, alleging he misled the Lok Sabha regarding Indian soldier deaths during Operation Sindoor. Venugopal cited the recent publication of six military personnel's names in the National War Memorial's Roll of Honour as contradiction. The defence ministry clarified that Singh's statement was a targeted response to a specific false narrative about lost pilots, and that the sacrifices of the soldiers had been acknowledged previously.
Content:
Congress leader KC Venugopal on Tuesday moved aprivilege noticeagainst Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in the Lok Sabha, alleging that he misled the House by stating during last year’s debate on Operation Sindoor that no Indian soldier had been killed during the military operation.

In a letter to Speaker Om Birla, Venugopal referred to Singh’s statement in the Lok Sabha on July 28, 2025, during the discussion on the Pahalgam terror attack and Operation Sindoor.

“If you have to ask a question, ask whether any harm came to our brave soldiers during this operation,” Singh had said. “The answer to that is no.”

Venugopal argued that the government’s recent disclosure of the names of six military personnel killed during Operation Sindoor contradicted Singh’s statement.

On June 26, thenamesof five Indian Army personnel and one Indian Air Force staffer who were killed during the operation were published in theRoll of Honoursection of the National War Memorial website. Their deaths had been previously acknowledged, and all six wereconferredwith gallantry awards in August 2025.

In his letter, Venugopal said that Singh’s statement in the House was “misleading and incorrect”.

He added: “It is well established that misleading the House or withholding information from the House by a minister on the floor of the House constitutes a breach of privilege and contempt of the House.”

After social media posts alleged that Singh had lied to Parliament, the Union government said on Saturday that the claims were “deliberately misleadingand factually incorrect”.

The defence ministry said that several social media posts “selectively quoted an isolated portion” of Singh’s July 2025 speech in Parliament to falsely imply that the minister claimed that no Indian soldiers were killed during the operation.

It added that Singh’s remark was in response to an “entirely false” narrative on media outlets and on social media that Indian pilots had been lost during Operation Sindoor.

“It was in direct reference to this specific and mischievous narrative that the [defence minister] made the statement in question,” the ministry said. “His remarks were, therefore, a targeted and contextually specific response to a falsehood that was gaining dangerous traction at that moment.”

On May 7, 2025, the Indian military carried outstrikeson what it claimed were terrorist camps in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir in response to the Pahalgam terror attack, which had killed 26 persons on April 22, 2025. The two sides had reached an “understanding” tohalt firingon May 10, 2025.

The six personnel whose names were published in theRoll of Honoursection of the National War Memorial website were Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Murali Naik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh and Air Force Sergeant Surendra Kumar.

On June 27, the Integrated Defence Staffclarifiedthat homage had been paid to the six personnel “at the earliest opportunity”, before the recent reports in the matter.

The military said that during a press conference on May 11, 2025, the director general of military operations had “paid solemn tribute to these brave soldiers and specifically acknowledged their sacrifice in the line of duty” during Operation Sindoor.

During the Army Day Parade on January 15, the Army chief had presented the Sena Medal (Gallantry) to the families of three of the personnel, the Integrated Defence Staff said in a statement. The Air Force chief had also done this in October at a ceremony.

Heading: Congress seeks privilege proceedings against Rajnath Singh, alleges House was misled on Operation Sindoor deaths
Summary: The Congress party has initiated breach of privilege proceedings against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of misleading Parliament in July 2025 by denying soldier deaths during Operation Sindoor, a claim contradicted by the recent inscription of six personnel's names at the National War Memorial. The party demands Singh's resignation and an apology from the Prime Minister, citing a grave insult to the armed forces and fallen personnel. The defence ministry, however, refutes these allegations, stating that Singh's speech was selectively quoted and that the nation appropriately honored the sacrifices.
Content:
The Congress on Tuesday stepped up its attack on Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of misleading Parliament over casualties suffered during Operation Sindoor and formally seeking breach of privilege proceedings against him in the Lok Sabha.
Senior Congress leader KC Venugopal submitted a notice to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla under Rule 223 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business, alleging that Singh's statement in Parliament in July last year was contradicted by the subsequent disclosure that six armed forces personnel lost their lives during the military operation.
The move comes days after the names of six personnel, five from the Indian Army and one from the Indian Air Force, were inscribed at the National War Memorial in New Delhi, marking the first official public disclosure of the soldiers who died during Operation Sindoor.
In a post on X, Venugopal alleged that the defence minister had made "a straightforward, clear-cut lie" while addressing Parliament.
"How could he, in July 2025, say that no Indian soldier was martyred, and then a year later the forces announce that we have lost six jawans?" he said.
Calling it "a grave insult" to the families of the fallen personnel and the armed forces, Venugopal said the soldiers "died in service of our nation while defending it against our enemies", but the government failed to acknowledge their sacrifice at the time.
In his notice to the Speaker, Venugopal argued that Singh's statement on the floor of the House was "clearly misleading and incorrect" in light of the later official confirmation of the deaths. He contended that providing incorrect information or withholding facts from Parliament amounts to a breach of privilege and contempt of the House, and urged the Speaker to initiate proceedings against the defence minister.
The Congress has also demanded Singh's resignation and sought an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
At a press conference on Monday, Congress' Ex-Servicemen Department chief Col Rohit Chaudhry (Retd) alleged that the BJP had "insulted" the armed forces by concealing the deaths of the six personnel.
"When Defence Minister Rajnath Singh was lying in Parliament that no soldier had been martyred, the BJP MPs were clapping. Rajnath Singh has insulted the country's army and soldiers -- we demand his resignation," Chaudhry said.
He also questioned why it took more than a year for the names of the six personnel to be publicly disclosed, while retired Wing Commander Anuma Acharya accused the government of departing from the long-standing tradition of publicly honouring soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice.
Responding to the controversy, the defence ministry has rejected allegations that Singh misled Parliament. It said certain social media posts had "selectively quoted an isolated portion" of the minister's July 2025 speech to create the false impression that he had claimed no Indian soldier died during Operation Sindoor.
The ministry maintained that the posts were "deliberately misleading and factually incorrect" and said the nation had paid tribute to the six personnel "at the earliest opportunity", adding that their sacrifice would always be honoured with "dignity and reverence".
Operation Sindoor was launched by India in May 2025 following the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people. During the operation, Indian forces struck terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir before responding to subsequent Pakistani military escalation.

Heading: Delayed Recognition
Summary: The article emphasizes a democracy's duty to honestly and promptly acknowledge its fallen soldiers, criticizing the delayed official recognition of casualties from Operation Sindoor. It argues that transparency in reporting combat losses builds public trust and reflects a confident nation, citing historical examples where India promptly honored its martyrs. The author concludes that fallen soldiers deserve open and timely recognition beyond just medals and memorials.
Content:
Every democracy owes two debts to its soldiers. The first is to equip them well enough to fight.
Every democracy owes two debts to its soldiers. The first is to equip them well enough to fight. The second is to acknowledge them with honesty if they fall. The first secures the nation’s borders. The second safeguards its conscience. The recent inscription of the names of six military personnel who died during Operation Sindoor at the National War Memorial has reopened questions that extend beyond party politics.
The issue is not whether these brave men were honoured. They were. They received gallantry awards, their families were presented with the medals, and they have now found a place on the nation’s Roll of Honour. The question is why a clear, official acknowledgement of their sacrifice as casualties of Operation Sindoor came only a year later. The government’s defence deserves consideration. It has pointed out that the Director General of Military Operations referred to casualties in May 2025, gallantry awards were announced in August, and the memorial inscription followed established protocol.
It has also clarified that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh’s statement in Parliament that no Indian soldiers had been harmed was intended to rebut claims that Indian fighter pilots had been killed during the operation. Yet the controversy has persisted because the minister’s recorded remarks were broader than that explanation. They conveyed the impression that India had suffered no military casualties. If a clarification becomes necessary a year later, it is reasonable to conclude that official communication left room for misunderstanding. This matters because democracies do not diminish military success by acknowledging combat losses. They reinforce public trust by doing so. No modern army can expect to wage operations without risk.
Soldiers know it, their families know it, and the nation knows it. What the public expects in return is candour once operational requirements have been met and next of kin have been informed. India has long understood this principle. During the Kargil conflict, casualty lists were released regularly and the nation watched as fallen soldiers were accorded military honours before being laid to rest. The Pulwama martyrs were identified immediately and mourned across the country. Other established democracies follow similar practices. Whether in the United States, the United Kingdom, Australia or Israel, operational details may remain classified, but the identities of personnel killed in action are normally made public after their families have been notified.
National remembrance is never treated as a military secret. The nation should not have had to piece together the human cost of a military campaign through local reports, medal citations and, eventually, inscriptions on a memorial wall. The strength of a democracy lies not in projecting an image of invulnerability but in possessing the confidence to acknowledge sacrifice with clarity and dignity. Those who lay down their lives for the Republic deserve not only medals and memorials, but also the simple honour of being named, openly and without delay. That is the least a grateful nation owes its fallen.

The names of the Indian Army soldiers who were martyred in this operation – Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Murali Naik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh, and Indian Air Force personnel Surendra Kumar – were inscribed on the National War Memorial wall in Delhi a few days ago. This was the first time the names of the soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor were released after the operation. A controversy has arisen over the release of names after a year.

In this context, the Congress has accused Defence Minister Rajnath Singh of misleading Parliament in the Operation Sindoor matter and has submitted a notice seeking privilege action against him under Rule 223 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha.

In a letter written to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Tuesday, senior Congress leader K.C. Venugopal stated, "A discussion was held in the Lok Sabha on July 28 last year regarding the Pahalgam terrorist attack and the subsequent Operation Sindoor. At that time, Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had stated that no Indian soldiers were harmed. Contrary to that statement, official information has been released with a list of names of 6 martyred soldiers. This clearly shows that the Defence Minister's statement that there were no casualties during Operation Sindoor was completely false."

"A minister misleading the House or concealing information is a breach of privilege and contempt of Parliament. Therefore, based on the notice submitted by the Congress in this matter, privilege action should be initiated against Rajnath Singh," he urged.

In an X post, K.C. Venugopal criticized, "Rajnath Singh has blatantly lied to the nation in the Lok Sabha discussion regarding Operation Sindoor. How did he state in 2025 (sic - likely a typo for 2023 or 2024) that no soldier was martyred? Now, the forces have announced that 6 soldiers were martyred. Not informing the public about the bravery and noble sacrifice of these 6 soldiers is a great insult to their families and the entire armed forces."

Attempt to Misrepresent: Ministry of Defence

The Ministry of Defence has clarified the controversies regarding the martyrdom of soldiers in Operation Sindoor.

"There has been no delay in paying tribute to the 6 martyrs on behalf of the nation; they will always be remembered with due dignity and respect.

Certain posts are being shared on social media, misrepresenting the Defence Minister's speech in Parliament on July 28 last year. A specific part of the speech has been quoted out of context to falsely portray that he stated no Indian soldier died in Operation Sindoor. Such malicious posts are false and completely untrue," the Ministry stated.

Summary: The Indian Ministry of Defense is moving to finalize a 30,000 crore rupees contract for 'Anant Shastra', a Quick Reaction Surface to Air Missile (QRSAM) developed by DRDO. This indigenous, truck-portable system, to be manufactured by BEL, is part of the multi-layered Integrated Air Defense Weapons System (IADWS) aimed at making India's air defense impenetrable. Content: Preparations began after the Sindoor campaign. A significant step is now being taken towards the preparation of the indigenous three-tier 'Sudarshan Chakra' (militarily known as 'Integrated Air Defense Weapons System' or IADWS) to make the air defense system impenetrable and robust. The Ministry of Defense has announced that a decision has been taken to finalize the contract for purchasing 'Anant Shastra', the 'Quick Reaction Surface to Air Missile' (QRSAM) developed by the Indian Defense Research and Development Organization (DRDO). The Defense Acquisition Council (DAC), led by Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, has already decided on a 30,000 crore rupees contract for the purchase of 'Anant Shastra'. The 'Acceptance of Necessity' for this has also been approved. The contract is expected to be finalized within the next few months. According to sources, the state-owned company 'Bharat Electronics Limited' (BEL) will manufacture 'Anant Shastra' in collaboration with DRDO. This truck-portable missile defense system can quickly target and destroy enemy drones, helicopters, aircraft, and even cruise missiles in the sky. Additionally, its ability to quickly change position makes it difficult for enemy missiles or rockets to target it. This QRSAM can accurately hit targets within a radius of approximately 30 kilometers, 10 kilometers above the ground. IADWS is essentially a multi-layered air defense system. This defense system includes Quick Reaction Surface to Air Missile (QRSAM), Advanced Very Short Air Defense System (VSHORADS), and Direct Energy Weapon (DEW). These three missile systems have made the new defense system even more agile and powerful. QRSAM can quickly target objects. This missile defense system will instantly destroy enemy missiles in the sky. VSHORADS can target short-range objects. This missile system will become active as soon as any danger is detected nearby. On the other hand, DEW is a state-of-the-art laser defense system. It will destroy any enemy weapon as soon as it enters the airspace. The country's new airspace defense system IADWS has been developed with these three systems.

Heading: KC Venugopal Files Privilege Motion Against Rajnath Singh Over Operation Sindoor Claims in Parliament
Summary: Congress MP KC Venugopal has filed a privilege motion against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, alleging he misled Parliament regarding casualties in Operation Sindoor. Content:
Congress MP KC Venugopal has submitted a privilege motion to Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla against Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. Venugopal filed the notice under Rule 223 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in Lok Sabha.

The dispute centres on Singh's claim that no Indian soldiers died during Operation Sindoor which contradicts the recent official naming of six military personnel killed in the conflict. The Alappuzha MP submitted the notice after the government publicly disclosed the identities of the fallen soldiers.

Venugopal outlined the specific timeline in his letter to the Speaker. "On July 28, 2025, during the discussion on the terrorist attack in Pahalgam and Operation Sindoor, the Minister of Defence inter alia stated as follows," Venugopal said.

The government recently inscribed the names of five Indian Army soldiers and one Indian Air Force personnel on a wall at the National War Memorial in Delhi. This marked the first public disclosure of their identities. Venugopal highlighted the discrepancy in parliamentary records.

"The aforementioned position clearly indicates that the Minister of Defence stating on the floor of the House that there had been no casualties during Operation Sindoor was clearly misleading and incorrect. It is well established that misleading the House or withholding information by a Minister on the Floor of the House constitutes a breach of privilege and contempt of the House," Venugopal said.

He sought strict action against the minister. "In view of the foregoing, I request that privilege proceedings may be initiated against the Minister of Defence in the matter," Venugopal added.

The Ministry of Defence clarified that social media platforms circulated distorted claims regarding Singh's statements. The ministry stated that these posts "selectively quoted an isolated portion of the speech to falsely imply that the defence minister claimed that no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor".

During his Lok Sabha address on July 28, 2025, Singh addressed the casualties directly. "If you want to raise a question, then ask whether any of our brave soldiers were harmed in this operation. The answer is, no, none of our soldiers were harmed," Singh said.

Singh dismissed Opposition queries regarding military aircraft losses, asserting that such questions do "not adequately represent our national sentiments." He emphasised that the focus should remain on the operation's success in destroying terror bases, noting that the military paused the mission only after achieving all politico-military objectives.

Indian forces launched Operation Sindoor on the night of May 6-7, 2025. The military targeted terror camps across Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. The strikes retaliated against the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack, which killed 26 people, primarily civilians.

The conflict concluded on May 10, 2025, when India accepted a ceasefire request from Pakistan. The government maintains that the operation is only paused.

‘Contempt of the House’

“The Minister’s statement on the floor of the House that there had been no casualties during Operation Sindoor was clearly misleading and incorrect,” Mr. Venugopal said in the notice, adding that misleading Parliament or withholding information amounted to a breach of privilege and contempt of the House.

In a post on X, Mr. Venugopal, who heads the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), alleged that Mr. Singh had “lied to the people of India” during the debate.

“How could he, in July 2025, say that no Indian soldier was martyred, and then a year later the forces announce that we have lost six jawans?” he asked.

Insult to the families

He said withholding information about the deaths was an insult to the families of the personnel and the armed forces, adding that they had laid down their lives in defence of the nation.

The controversy erupted after the names of six personnel — five from the Indian Army and one from the Indian Air Force — who died during Operation Sindoor were inscribed on the National War Memorial, marking the first official disclosure of the casualties since the operation was carried out in May 2025.

Rejecting the Opposition’s allegations, the Defence Ministry said the nation had honoured the fallen personnel at the “earliest opportunity” and that their sacrifice would always be remembered with dignity and reverence.

It also accused “certain posts circulating on social media” of selectively quoting Mr. Singh’s July 28 speech to falsely suggest that he had claimed no Indian soldier had lost his life during Operation Sindoor, describing such claims as “deliberately misleading and factually incorrect”.

Operation Sindoor was launched in response to the April 22, 2025, terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 people, mostly civilians, were killed.

Heading: From Sainik School to Army Chief: General Upendra Dwivedi said in an emotional farewell - the strength of the army is its soldiers
Summary: General Upendra Dwivedi, before concluding his tenure as Army Chief, paid tribute to martyrs and reflected on his four-decade military career, calling service in the Indian Army his greatest privilege. He emphasized that the army's strength lies in the trust of its soldiers, veterans, families, and countrymen, not just one officer. Dwivedi highlighted the army's vigilance on all fronts, including 'Operation Snow Leopard' and 'Operation Sindoor', and stressed the need for joint operations among the three forces for future warfare, as he handed over command to General Dheeraj Seth.
Content:
General Upendra Dwivedi: Before stepping down as Army Chief, General Upendra Dwivedi paid tribute to the martyrs by laying a wreath at the National War Memorial in Delhi on Tuesday. In the farewell ceremony held thereafter, he recalled his four-decade-long military life. According to ANI news agency, he said that serving in the Indian Army has been the greatest privilege of his life.
In his address, General Dwivedi said that the true strength of the Indian Army lies not in any one officer, but in the trust of its soldiers, commanders, veterans, families, and countrymen. He saluted all the soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice while defending the country. He said that his journey from Sainik School to becoming the Army Chief has been unforgettable for him.
General Dwivedi said that in the last two years, the Indian Army maintained readiness, balance, and vigilance on every front. Strong deployment was maintained on the northern borders under 'Operation Snow Leopard', while on the western front, the army fulfilled its responsibilities with restraint and seriousness. He cited 'Operation Sindoor' as a prime example of this.
General Upendra Dwivedi stated that future warfare will be joint and theater-based, hence better coordination between the Army, Navy, and Air Force is essential. He gave a message to all three forces: 'See together, decide together, and act together.'
At the end of the farewell, General Upendra Dwivedi handed over the command of the Army Chief to General Dheeraj Seth, stating that General Seth is an experienced and capable leader. He said that under General Seth's leadership, the Indian Army will reach new heights and carry forward its glorious traditions.

Heading: General Dwivedi retires from Army Chief post: Said - Army fulfilled responsibilities well, Operation Sindoor an example; New General Dheeraj Seth takes charge

Content:
General Upendra Dwivedi retired from the post of Army Chief on Tuesday. Before retirement, he paid tribute to the martyred soldiers at the National War Memorial in New Delhi.
Dwivedi said - In two years, the Indian Army maintained its preparedness, balance, and vigilance on every front. Operation Sindoor is a prime example of this.
He said that today I am handing over this responsibility to General Dheeraj Seth. He is an experienced soldier and a capable leader. I am fully confident that under his leadership, the Indian Army will reach new heights while upholding its glorious traditions.
General Dheeraj Seth has replaced Dwivedi. He took charge today. Seth is India's 31st Army Chief. He has almost four decades of experience in the Indian Army. He joined the army in December 1986.
General Dwivedi said - The Indian Army maintained preparedness on every front.
General Seth has served as Deputy Army Chief.
Seth comes from an army background family.
Army Chief Seth comes from an army background family. His father, Lieutenant General Krishna Mohan Seth, retired from the Indian Army as Adjutant General in 1997.
General Krishna Mohan Seth also commanded two large and important units of the army, XXI Strike Corps and III Corps. Dheeraj Seth also has a deep interest in sports. He likes to play tennis and golf. His wife's name is Komal Seth.
The names of 6 martyrs of Operation Sindoor made public for the first time: 5 Army, 1 Air Force personnel, 2 received gallantry awards; names registered in War Memorial.

Heading: GWMC polls are semi-finals, BJP chief Nitin Nabin tells Telangana party workers
Summary: BJP national president Nitin Nabin addressed party workers in Hanamkonda, framing the upcoming GWMC polls as crucial for establishing a 'double engine sarkar' in Telangana by 2028. Nabin assured the people that the BJP government would work to fulfill their dreams under PM Modi's leadership.
Content:
HANAMKONDA: Terming the forthcoming Greater Warangal Municipal Corporation (GWMC) elections as the semi-finals and the 2028 Assembly elections as the finals, BJP national president Nitin Nabin called upon the people of Telangana to work towards establishing a ‘double engine sarkar’ in the state.

Highlighting the party’s decades-long association with the state, Nabin recalled that when the BJP had won only two Lok Sabha seats in the country, one was from Telangana.

He addressed a meeting of booth-level presidents at the Arts & Science College grounds in Hanamkonda on Monday. BJP Telangana president N Ramchander Rao, Union Minister G Kishan Reddy, Minister of State Bandi Sanjay, MPs and other party leaders were present.

Nabin said Prime Minister Narendra Modi was working round the clock for the nation, while Congress leader Rahul Gandhi was only a part-time politician. Referring to the Telangana statehood movement, he alleged that the Congress had not supported the demand for a separate state for a long time, while late MP Sushma Swaraj had strongly backed Telangana in Parliament.

He claimed that the Congress eventually introduced the Telangana Bill in Parliament with the BJP’s support.

The saffron party chief also said the BJP-led Union government had allocated crores for Telangana’s development over the past 12 years.

Referring to projects in Warangal, Nabin said the long-pending Railway Manufacturing Unit at Kazipet had been sanctioned and would begin operations soon.

‘Congress failed to provide two lakh jobs’

Nabin alleged that the project, first proposed during the tenure of late Prime Minister P V Narasimha Rao, had been delayed due to Congress.

Nabin also criticised the Congress over the treatment of late prime minister PV Narasimha Rao after his death, alleging that the party blocked public display of the body in Delhi and did not allow his family to construct a memorial in the nation’s capital. He said the BJP-led Union government had later honoured Narasimha Rao with the Bharat Ratna.

Alleging that the Congress had failed to fulfil its promise of providing two lakh government jobs, Nabin claimed the party had turned Telangana into an ATM for its leadership in Delhi.

“The dreams of the people of Telangana have been lost in the quagmire of family-based parties. Therefore, we are committed to fulfilling the dreams of the people of Telangana,” the BJP national president said.

“I have come to assure the youth, farmers, and women of Telangana that the BJP government, under the leadership of PM Modi, works for you and works for the people. In the coming days, by standing with your struggles, the BJP will form a ‘double-engine’ government here and fulfil every dream of the people of Telangana,” he declared.

Nabin said India’s internal and external security had been strengthened under the BJP government over the past 12 years. He said India had responded firmly to cross-border terrorism through surgical strikes, air strikes and Operation Sindoor. He also claimed the government had taken decisive steps to eliminate Naxalism and said the aspirations of the people of Telangana could be realised under Modi’s leadership.

He said the Union government had demonstrated its commitment to Warangal’s development by sanctioning funds for the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park, the Kazipet Railway Manufacturing Unit, Mamnoor Airport, National Highways and the Tribal University.

Later, Nitin Nabin visited the Bhadrakali temple and offered special prayers.

Heading: Congress seeks Rajnath Singh’s resignation in controversy over Operation Sindoor deaths
