The opposition alleges the government concealed the deaths of six military personnel for over a year, denying them due recognition and politicizing the armed forces. The government, however, refutes these claims, stating it honored the fallen personnel at the earliest opportunity and that critics are misquoting the Defence Minister.
Content:
Stepping up its attack on the Centre over the deaths of six military personnel during Operation Sindoor, the Congress on Monday (June 29, 2026) demanded the resignation of Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of “lying” in Parliament by stating that no Indian soldier had been killed in the operation.

The party also demanded an apology from Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Congress accuses Rajnath Singh of misleading Parliament on Operation Sindoor casualties

Addressing a press conference, chairperson of the Congress’s Ex-servicemen Department Col. Rohit Chaudhry (Retd.) and Wing Commander Anuma Acharya (Retd.) alleged that by concealing the deaths of six personnel — five from the Indian Army and one from the Indian Air Force — during the May 2025 operation, the Narendra Modi government had denied them due public recognition and honour.

Wing Commander Acharya claimed that previous governments had publicly honoured every soldier who made the supreme sacrifice, and accused the present dispensation of “politicising the armed forces”.

Why it took nearly a year for Operation Sindoor martyrs’ names to reach the National War Memorial

“The Modi government, which politicises the army and soldiers, has repeatedly betrayed the country and the soldiers,” she said.

Col. Chaudhry accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of using “soldiers as props” while seeking votes in the name of the armed forces.

Centre debunks social media claims over Rajnath Singh’s Operation Sindoor speech

“When Defence Minister Rajnath Singh was lying in Parliament that no soldier had been martyred, BJP MPs were clapping. Rajnath Singh has insulted the country’s army and soldiers. We demand his resignation,” Col. Chaudhry said.

Mr. Singh had “insulted” the soldiers who laid down their lives during Operation Sindoor, he alleged, and questioned why it had taken 13 months for their names to be made public.

“The foundation of the Modi government is built on lies. They have no right to remain in power,” he said.

Listing the party’s demands, Col. Chaudhry said the Congress would urge its leadership to move a breach of privilege motion against the Defence Minister.

He also called on Mr. Modi and BJP MPs to publicly apologise for backing what he described as Mr. Singh’s “lies”, and reiterated the Congress’s demand for the scrapping of the Agnipath recruitment scheme.

The controversy intensified after the government recently disclosed the names of the martyred soldiers, when they were inscribed on the National War Memorial, more than a year after the operation.

The government has rejected the Opposition’s charge, maintaining that the nation had paid tribute to the fallen personnel at the “earliest opportunity”, and that their memory has been honoured with the dignity and reverence it deserves.

The Defence Ministry has also accused critics of selectively quoting Mr. Singh’s statement in Parliament in July 2025 to falsely suggest that he had claimed no Indian soldier had died during Operation Sindoor. Social media posts had misrepresented the Minister’s remarks by taking them out of context, the Defence Ministry said.

Heading: Disrespect towards those who attained martyrdom
Summary: The Central Government faced criticism for a year-long delay in officially releasing the names of six soldiers martyred in 'Operation Sindoor', a retaliatory action against the 2025 Pahalgam terrorist attack. Despite earlier parliamentary discussions where the Defence Minister claimed no Indian casualties, the government eventually inscribed the names on the National War Memorial, prompting accusations from opposition parties of disrespect and a deliberate cover-up to protect the Prime Minister's image. The article questions the government's narrative and motives behind the delayed recognition.
Content: The Central Government recently officially released the details of the soldiers who attained martyrdom in 'Operation Sindoor', conducted by the Indian Army in retaliation for the Pahalgam terrorist attack. The delay in releasing the names of the brave jawans who sacrificed their lives for the country has drawn criticism. The criticism is that there has been disrespect towards the soldiers and a delay in providing them due recognition. The terrorist attack in Pahalgam, Kashmir, occurred on April 22, 2025, resulting in the loss of 26 civilian lives. It was the nation's collective interest to deliver a strong blow to those responsible for such a major terrorist attack. Subsequently, the Indian Army launched 'Operation Sindoor' in the early hours of May 7. The forces destroyed nine bases of terrorist organizations in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir. Military operations concluded on May 10. There has been no convincing response from Indian authorities to repeated claims by Modi's friend, US President Donald Trump, that the cessation of military operations was a result of his intervention. A press release issued by the Press Information Bureau regarding 'Operation Sindoor' stated that hundreds of terrorists were killed in the attack. However, there was no mention of Indian soldiers attaining martyrdom. Furthermore, when the issue, including the Pahalgam terrorist attack and Operation Sindoor, was discussed in Parliament in July 2025, neither the Prime Minister nor the ministers were willing to mention it. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh even made statements suggesting there were no casualties on the Indian side. In response to questions raised by the opposition, the Defence Minister stated in the Lok Sabha, “The answer to the question, 'Has the army dealt with the terrorists who wiped out the sindoor of our sisters and daughters in Operation Sindoor, and have their masters been eliminated?' is yes. The answer to the question, 'Have any of our brave soldiers been injured in this operation?' is no, none of our soldiers were injured.” It was almost a year later that the Central Government announced that six soldiers lost their lives in 'Operation Sindoor', including their names in the 'Roll of Honour' section of the National War Memorial in New Delhi. Their names were also engraved on the memorial wall. The main criticism is that this action eliminates the opportunity to pay due respect to the martyred jawans. The CPI stated that it was shameful that the BJP government took a year to officially announce the names of those who attained martyrdom. The Prime Minister did not mention them or their sacrifice in his speech during the special session of Parliament. Other opposition parties also accuse a government that boasts about nationalism of shamefully denying due recognition to brave jawans for over a year. When the incident became controversial, the Central Defence Ministry claimed that the soldiers had already been honored. It was stated that their names were included in the list of those honored on Independence Day 2025. This raises pertinent questions: if their names were included among hundreds of others receiving various honors, would it truly be recognition for martyrdom in 'Operation Sindoor', an action acknowledged by the people and, as the Centre claims, the whole world? And if such a step had been taken earlier, why did the BJP not celebrate it? The government also stated that it was factually incorrect that the Defence Minister misled the Lok Sabha. Even after this explanation, excerpts from Rajnath Singh's parliamentary speech continue to circulate on social media. This action comes from a government that routinely engages in rhetoric about patriotism and soldiers. This is where the crucial question arises: why was the martyrdom of soldiers hidden for so long? It must be assumed that it was deliberately concealed out of concern that the glory of the Prime Minister and others might diminish if the martyrdom of the soldiers were honored. Here, the cunning strategy of the BJP, which places the idol of Modi above all else and celebrates it, is exposed.

Heading: Congress Seeks Rajnath Singh's Removal over 'No Martyr' Remark on Operation Sindoor
Summary: The Congress party has demanded the removal of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of misleading Parliament by claiming no Indian soldier was martyred during Operation Sindoor and insulting fallen soldiers. They allege ten soldiers died, with four names still missing, and link the operation's context to a major security failure in the Pahalgam terror attack. The party also criticized the government's handling of the operation, citing weak diplomacy and political pressure, and reiterated its call to abolish the Agnipath recruitment scheme.
Content:
The Congress has demanded the removal of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, accusing him of misleading Parliament by claiming that no Indian soldier was martyred during Operation Sindoor. The party called the remark an insult to the country's fallen soldiers and said it would pursue a privilege motion against him.

Addressing a press conference at party headquarters in New Delhi on Sunday, Colonel Rohit Chaudhary, chairman of the Congress's ex servicemen department, and retired Wing Commander Anuma Acharya said Singh had made a false statement in Parliament on 28 July 2025 regarding casualties from the operation. They demanded an apology from the Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the Defence Minister and the BJP leadership to the families of the martyrs, the armed forces and the nation, and repeated the party's call for the Agnipath recruitment scheme to be scrapped entirely.

The leaders also questioned why it took thirteen months for the names of soldiers killed during the operation, which concluded in May 2025, to be made public, calling it a compromise on national security. Chaudhary claimed ten soldiers had died during the operation, adding that while six names had recently been added to the National War Memorial website and the memorial at India Gate, four remained missing.

The party also linked the operation's background to the Pahalgam terror attack, which Chaudhary described as a major security failure falling under the Centre's responsibility given Jammu and Kashmir's status as a Union Territory. He alleged that intelligence agencies under the Union Home Ministry had ignored prior warnings, noting that Home Minister Amit Shah had reviewed security between 6 and 8 April 2025 shortly before the attack occurred. Chaudhary further argued that India had missed a chance to reclaim Pakistan occupied Kashmir owing to weak diplomacy, while Pakistan gained diplomatically and financially in the aftermath.

Acharya criticised the government's conduct of the operation, saying External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar's early assurance that India would strike only terrorist infrastructure had cost the air force the element of surprise. She cited remarks attributed to Chief of Defence Staff General Anil Chauhan and a defence attache in Jakarta to suggest political pressure had contributed to damage to Indian aircraft, and criticised the eventual ceasefire following intervention by US President Donald Trump.

The Congress also raised concerns over unequal benefits for Agniveer families, saying the scheme would be abolished if the party returned to power.

Heading: Congress demands Rajnath Singh’s resignation over Operation Sindoor martyrs row
Summary: The Congress party has demanded Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's resignation and Prime Minister Narendra Modi's apology, accusing them of misleading Parliament and delaying the honoring of six personnel martyred during 'Operation Sindoor'. The opposition claims this constitutes an 'insult to soldiers' and seeks the abolition of the Agniveer scheme. The defence ministry, however, asserts that the nation paid homage at the earliest opportunity and the martyrs' memory will be honored.
Content:
The Congress accused Defence Minister Rajnath Singh of misleading Parliament over casualties during Operation Sindoor and demanded his resignation. The party also sought Prime Minister Narendra Modi's apology, alleging the government delayed honouring six personnel who died during the operation

New Delhi: The Congress on Monday alleged that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh “lied” in Parliament that no soldier had been “martyred” during Operation Sindoor and demanded his resignation as well as Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s apology over the issue.

The opposition party has accused the government of concealing the supreme sacrifice of six soldiers during Operation Sindoor and thus denying them the honour, in what it claimed was an “insult to our soldiers”.

Congress’ Ex-Servicemen Department chief Col Rohit Chaudhry (retd) alleged that the BJP talks about soldiers, but uses them as a prop to fire guns, seeks votes in the name of martyrs, and “insults them”.

“When Defence Minister Rajnath Singh was lying in Parliament that no soldier had been martyred, the BJP MPs were clapping. None of these people have the right to sit in the House. Rajnath Singh has insulted the country’s army and soldiers — we demand his resignation,” Chaudhry said at a press conference along with Wing Commander Anuma Acharya (retd).

The names of six military personnel — five from the Indian Army and one from IAF — who died in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor last year, was recently inscribed on a wall at the National War Memorial, as a tribute to the fallen heroes. This was the first time since the military operation conducted by the Indian armed forces in May 2025 that the government released the names of these six personnel.

Amid the row surrounding the six martyrs of Operation Sindoor, the defence ministry has said the nation paid homage to them at the “earliest opportunity”, and their memory shall always be honoured with the dignity and reverence it deserves.

The government had earlier said some social media posts sought to “misrepresent” Defence Minister Singh’s address in Parliament in July 2025 and “selectively” quoted an isolated portion of it to “falsely imply” that he had claimed that “no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor”. In his remarks at the presser, Chaudhry claimed that Singh has “insulted” the martyrs of ‘Operation Sindoor’ and overlooked them.

“Singh lied in the House that no soldier was lost in ‘Operation Sindoor’. Inside the BJP, only lies are told and deception is carried out…The foundation of the Modi government is built on lies; they have no right to remain in power,” Chaudhry said.

The country is asking why it took 13 months for the names of our martyred soldiers to come to the fore, he said. Putting forward the Congress’ demands, Chaudhry said, “Our demands — Defence Minister Rajnath Singh should be removed from his position. We urge our party to bring a breach of privilege motion against the defence minister. PM Narendra Modi and BJP MPs should publicly apologize for supporting Rajnath Singh’s lies. Also, the Agniveer scheme should be completely abolished.”

Acharya said that before the BJP government came to power, there was a tradition that whoever made the supreme sacrifice for the country was publicly honoured with gratitude.

“But the Modi government, which politicizes the army and soldiers, has repeatedly betrayed the country and the soldiers,” she said.

Heading: We don't give importance to these meetings! New Delhi responds to the India-Pakistan 'Track 2 dialogue' controversy in Colombo
Summary: India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri clarified New Delhi's stance on a recent 'Track 2 dialogue' in Colombo involving retired Indian and Pakistani officials, stating that the Indian government does not give importance to such privately organized meetings and has no connection or support for them. He emphasized that any Indian participants were expressing personal views, not officially representing the government, especially given the deteriorated India-Pakistan relations due to terrorism.
Content: The meeting held in the capital of Sri Lanka was organized entirely on a private initiative. The retired diplomats and military officials who participated in it have no connection with the Government of India. New Delhi does not give any importance to such meetings. India's Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri made this clear on Monday. Relations between India and Pakistan have further deteriorated since the Pahalgam attack and the Sindoor operation. New Delhi has repeatedly blamed Islamabad on international platforms, including the United Nations, for supporting terrorism. Amidst this, news recently spread that a team of experts comprising retired military and diplomatic officials from India and Pakistan held a meeting in Colombo, the capital of Sri Lanka, last week. Various sources claimed that several countries, including India, Pakistan, Sri Lanka, Maldives, and Britain, were present at the conference of the 'International Institute for Strategic Studies'. Retired officials from India and Pakistan held discussions in a side meeting of the conference. Since the news of that meeting spread, speculation about 'Track 2 diplomacy' (private-level discussions between two conflicting countries, where government officials are not present) between the two countries increased. Now, New Delhi has clarified its position on this controversy. Foreign Secretary Misri is currently on a visit to Seychelles with Prime Minister Modi. On Monday, he issued a statement regarding the Colombo meeting from there. In response to journalists' questions, the Foreign Secretary said, "Many such events on various topics are organized in different parts of the world. There is nothing new or special about such discussions. For us, these are just private events organized on private initiative. None of these have any official basis." It is noteworthy that retired officials from both India and Pakistan were reportedly present at the Colombo meeting. Regarding this, the Foreign Secretary said, "I cannot comment on behalf of the Government of Pakistan. But speaking for the Government of India, there was no officially authorized representation in this discussion. The Government of India has no connection or support for it." He further added, "Whether they are retired diplomats, retired military officials, or members of civil society, those from India who participate in such events are presenting their personal opinions and perspectives. The Government of India does not give importance to such matters."

Heading: Mann Ki Baat: 'Mann Ki Baat' or 'Secrets of the Mind'? What does the 'Modi Government' want to achieve by ignoring burning issues?
Summary: The article critically examines the Modi government's struggle to maintain its public image despite a strong political position, highlighting a perceived gap between PM Modi's 'Mann Ki Baat' and addressing pressing national issues. It cites journalist Dr. A. Suryaprakash's critique, which points to a lack of energy and arrogance among many central ministers and BJP chief ministers, alongside various allegations of corruption and inefficiency. The piece concludes that significant changes within the government, party, and key institutions are essential to restore public trust, which is currently eroding due to the shortcomings of trusted colleagues.
Content:
Narendra Modi Government: Despite being in a strong position, Prime Minister Modi and the BJP are finding it difficult to maintain their public image after twelve years.
Sunil Chavke
Prime Minister Narendra Modi has been sharing 'Mann Ki Baat' with the countrymen for 135 consecutive weeks. But most of the time, the real, inner thoughts are not revealed. He usually avoids commenting on burning issues in the country. After coming to power for the third time, the Prime Minister might not have been able to elaborate on the performance of his cabinet colleagues in 'Mann Ki Baat', even if he wished to. Moreover, in the last twelve years, a person from the family or associated with the family has rarely dared to advise the Prime Minister on what direction the Modi government should take. But such an initiative has been taken by journalist-writer Dr. A. Suryaprakash through an article.
Dr. A. Suryaprakash, who served as the Chairman of 'Prasar Bharati' from 2014 to 2020, was honored with 'Padma Bhushan' last year, is a fellow at 'Vivekananda International Foundation', and currently a member of the Prime Minister's Museum and Library Society, is a senior journalist held in high regard in Delhi's political and Sangh-BJP circles. Therefore, there is scope to conclude that the Prime Minister might have tried to admonish his cabinet colleagues through Suryaprakash without revealing his own thoughts.
"Although Modi's performance as Prime Minister for twelve years has been extraordinary, most central ministers have failed to show comparable energy in their work. Arrogance is evident in the behavior and speech of many central ministers and chief ministers of BJP-ruled states. The BJP, the world's largest political party with fourteen crore members, has national general secretaries or office bearers who are not very well-known and have failed to energize the workers," Suryaprakash has stated.
While attributing all the credit for the central government and BJP's twelve years of success to Prime Minister Modi, Suryaprakash has subtly conveyed Modi's inner thoughts, stating that the Prime Minister is facing the problem of the quality of his central cabinet colleagues and the growing fatigue and lethargy within the party. He has emphasized the need for a political surgery by giving opportunities to new blood to maintain the central government and BJP's diminishing influence on the countrymen.
The discussion about cabinet reshuffle, which began even before the central government completed twelve years on June 10, has taken a new turn due to this article. It is also being said that apart from Union Home and Cooperation Minister Amit Shah, no one else truly matters in Modi's 71-member central cabinet.
Despite presenting nine central budgets consecutively since 2019, including eight full and one interim, Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman has not been able to properly stabilize the country's economy. Not a single budget presented by her has been memorable.
During the tenure of S. Jaishankar, who has served as External Affairs Minister for more than seven years, there is an outcry within the BJP itself that foreign policy has declined on all fronts. Dharmendra Pradhan will complete five years as the country's Education Minister next week. During this period, opposition parties allege that 65 to 89 incidents of paper leaks in various examinations have occurred across the country.
The most important question in the reshuffle discussion is whether Dharmendra Pradhan will be removed. Hardeep Singh Puri, who manages the Petroleum Ministry, which is very sensitive from the perspective of the country's fuel security, is embroiled in the 'Epstein Files' controversy. Although Defense Minister Rajnath Singh has not been very controversial, he drew criticism for making a false statement in Parliament by emphatically stating, without being asked, that there was no loss of life in India during 'Operation Sindoor'.
Minister of State for Agriculture Bhagirath Chaudhary has raised questions about the transparent functioning of the Modi government by allegedly misappropriating 99 lakh rupees from his own ministry's scheme for his own farm. Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav's family members are accused of purchasing 168 acres of land in Ujjain in areas where highway and road projects are proposed.
Apart from Mohan Yadav, the Supreme Court has also ordered a CBI inquiry into allegations of corruption amounting to about one thousand two hundred seventy crores against Arunachal Pradesh Chief Minister Pema Khandu and his family members in government contracts.
Uttarakhand Chief Minister Pushkar Dhami is surrounded by allegations of corruption, recruitment irregularities, and the Ankita Bhandari case. The tenures of Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi, Rajasthan Chief Minister Bhajanlal Sharma, and Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai have been completely ineffective. In Uttar Pradesh, the alleged latent power struggle between Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the BJP high command seems to be decided only in the assembly elections.
The revelation of the theft of thousands of crores of donations at the Ram Mandir in Ayodhya has deeply hurt the faith of millions of devotees. This led to the resignation of Champat Rai, General Secretary, and Anil Mishra, Trustee, of the 'Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Trust'. As per the Supreme Court's directive, Prime Minister Modi himself announced the 'Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Nyas' in the Lok Sabha on February 5, 2020.
But after the donation theft case came to light, the Trust showed arrogance by refusing to provide accounts requested by the Prime Minister's Office. After the assembly elections in five states, the Modi government, which split the Trinamool Congress and Shiv Sena-Uddhav Balasaheb Thackeray party to gain 26 MPs in the Lok Sabha, is now focused on securing the support of 22 DMK MPs and splitting 25 out of 37 Samajwadi Party MPs. This will enable the BJP to easily pass any constitutional amendment bill in Parliament.
Despite being in a strong position with a two-thirds majority in both Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha, power in 21 out of 31 states, and a completely fragmented opposition, Prime Minister Modi and the BJP are finding it difficult to maintain their public image after twelve years.
The public perception of the government and the BJP is eroding due to the inefficient and corrupt tendencies of the ministers, chief ministers, and leaders of important institutions chosen and fully trusted by the Prime Minister himself. How the necessary and expected widespread changes in the government, party organization, and key institutions are carried out to rectify this will be crucial.

Heading: 'Rajnath Singh should resign', accused of misleading Parliament on Operation Sindoor, BK Hariprasad demands accountability
Summary: Karnataka Congress chief BK Hariprasad demanded Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's resignation, accusing him of misleading Parliament regarding casualties in 'Operation Sindoor' by contradicting his 2025 statement with the recent inscription of six martyrs' names at the National War Memorial. The Defence Ministry clarified that these sacrifices were honored previously through press conferences and gallantry awards, rejecting claims of recent first-time acknowledgment.
Content:
Karnataka Congress chief BK Hariprasad on Monday (June 29, 2026) demanded the resignation of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh. He made this demand amidst the recent controversy over the names of six military personnel martyred during 'Operation Sindoor'. The names of these six soldiers have recently been inscribed on the National War Memorial.

BK Hariprasad, in a post on 'X', cited a statement made by Defence Minister Rajnath Singh in Parliament in 2025. He claimed that the Defence Minister had clearly stated that no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor.

He said that the subsequent public disclosure of the names of military personnel martyred during the operation reveals a serious contradiction between the Defence Minister's earlier statement and the information that later emerged.

Hariprasad wrote on 'X', "Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had clearly stated in Parliament that #OperationSindoor during which no Indian soldier lost his life. But the BJP government's subsequent disclosure of the names of the military personnel who made the supreme sacrifice exposes a serious contradiction in his earlier statement."

Hariprasad further said, "If Parliament has been misled on such a serious issue of national importance, accountability cannot be avoided. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh should resign for misleading Parliament. Our martyrs deserve truth, honesty, and respect, not contradictory statements."

Defence Minister @rajnathsingh categorically had told Parliament that no Indian soldiers had lost their lives during #OperationSindoor. The @BJP4IndiaGovt's own subsequent disclosure naming the personnel who made the supreme sacrifice exposes a serious contradiction. If…

It should be noted that the names of six Indian security force personnel martyred during 'Operation Sindoor', which lasted for four days against Pakistan in May 2025, have now been inscribed on the National War Memorial in New Delhi.

As politics heated up on this issue, the Ministry of Defence clarified on Saturday that the nation had already honored the six military personnel who made the supreme sacrifice during Operation Sindoor at the appropriate time. The Ministry rejected claims that their sacrifice was publicly acknowledged for the first time recently.

The Defence Ministry's release stated, "Some reports circulating in certain sections of the media and on social media platforms have falsely claimed that the sacrifice of the six brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during Operation Sindoor has been acknowledged or made public for the first time recently. It is clarified that these martyrs were paid tribute by the nation much before the related reports emerged, at the earliest available opportunity."

According to the release, during an official press conference held on May 11, 2025, the then Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) paid tribute to these brave soldiers and specifically mentioned their supreme sacrifice while performing duty during Operation Sindoor.

Furthermore, these brave soldiers were also honored with gallantry awards, the information of which was made public in an official press release on August 14, 2025. The Ministry stated that this was a formal and national-level recognition of their valor and supreme sacrifice, in line with the highest traditions of the Indian Armed Forces.

The Government of India has officially made public the names of 6 soldiers martyred during Operation Sindoor for the first time. The names of these brave soldiers will be inscribed in the Roll of Honor on the website of the National War Memorial in Delhi. India had launched Operation Sindoor on the night of May 6 and 7, 2025, to destroy terrorist bases located in Pakistan.

Heading: Political Storm Brews Over Alleged Misleading Claims by Defence Minister
Summary: A political controversy has erupted in Karnataka, with Congress chief BK Hariprasad demanding Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's resignation. Hariprasad alleges that Singh misled Parliament in 2025 by denying soldier fatalities during 'Operation Sindoor,' a claim now contradicted by the BJP government's recent acknowledgment of six fallen soldiers. The Defence Ministry, however, clarified that tributes and gallantry honors for these heroes were timely, countering suggestions of delayed recognition.
Content:
Karnataka Congress chief BK Hariprasad on Monday called for the resignation of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, amid controversy over the acknowledgment of fallen soldiers during 'Operation Sindoor.' Hariprasad's demands followed Singh's 2025 parliamentary statement, claiming no soldier fatalities during the operation, now contradicted by recent disclosures.

The Congress leader stated on X that Singh's statement misled Parliament by denying soldier casualties, a contradiction exposed by the BJP government's recent acknowledgment of six soldiers who died during the operation. 'If Parliament was misled on such national importance, accountability cannot be avoided,' Hariprasad asserted, demanding Singh's resignation for misleading lawmakers.

The Defence Ministry clarified that tributes to the fallen heroes were timely, counteracting reports suggesting their sacrifice was only recently recognized. During a May 2025 press conference, the Director General of Military Operations paid homage to the soldiers, acknowledging their courage and awarding them gallantry honors as a testament to their sacrifice.

Heading: BK Hariprasad demands Rajnath Singh's resignation, says accountability cannot be avoided for "misleading" Parliament on Op Sindoor
Summary: Karnataka Congress chief BK Hariprasad has demanded Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's resignation, accusing him of misleading Parliament regarding casualties in "Operation Sindoor" after six fallen personnel's names were etched at the National War Memorial. The Ministry of Defence, however, clarified that these sacrifices were formally acknowledged and awarded in 2025, refuting claims of recent public disclosure.
Content: Bengaluru (Karnataka) [India], June 29 (ANI): Karnataka Congress chief BK Hariprasad on Monday demanded the resignation of Defence Minister Rajnath Singh amid the recent controversy surrounding the names of six armed forces personnel who lost their lives during "Operation Sindoor," which were recently etched at the National War Memorial. In a post on 'X', Hariprasad referenced Rajnath Singh's 2025 parliamentary speech, claiming the Defence Minister had "categorically" told Parliament that no soldiers' lives were lost during Operation Sindoor. He stressed that the subsequent disclosure of the operation's fallen heroes represents a "serious contradiction" to the Minister's earlier remarks. "Defence Minister Rajnath Singh categorically told Parliament that no Indian soldiers lost their lives during #OperationSindoor. The BJP government's own subsequent disclosure naming the personnel who made the supreme sacrifice exposes a serious contradiction," the Congress leader wrote on X. "If Parliament was misled on a matter of such national importance, accountability cannot be avoided. Rajnath Singh must resign for misleading Parliament. Our martyrs deserve truth, honesty, and respect--not contradictory statements," Hariprasad added. The names of the six Indian security personnel who died during the four-day operation against Pakistan in May 2025 have since been etched at the National War Memorial in New Delhi. As the issue ignited a political row, the Ministry of Defence clarified on Saturday that the nation had honoured the six personnel who made the supreme sacrifice during Operation Sindoor at the earliest opportunity, rejecting claims that their sacrifice had only been acknowledged publicly for the "first time" recently. According to the release, it stated, "Certain reports circulating in sections of the media and on social media platforms have incorrectly suggested that the supreme sacrifice of six bravehearts during Operation Sindoor has been acknowledged or brought to public notice for the first time only recently. It is clarified that the nation paid homage to these fallen heroes at the earliest opportunity, well before the reports in question." During the official press conference held on May 11, 2025, the then Director General of Military Operations paid solemn tribute to these brave soldiers and specifically acknowledged their sacrifice in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor. These bravehearts were conferred with gallantry awards, and this was published in the press release of August 14, 2025. This constituted a formal and national recognition of their valour and supreme sacrifice in keeping with the highest traditions of the Indian Defence Forces, the release had stated. (ANI)

Heading: Writings On A Wall
Summary: The article criticizes the Indian government for delaying the acknowledgement of soldiers killed in Operation Sindoor and for a broader pattern of concealing facts regarding military casualties and other national events. It argues that such lack of transparency, exemplified by past incidents like the Balakot airstrikes and the Bahanaga train crash, erodes public trust and disrespects the sacrifices of soldiers. The author advocates for prompt and dignified recognition for fallen soldiers and complete transparency from the government to uphold democratic values and ensure accountability.
Content:
A nation remembers its wars not only through victories but also through the names of those who never returned to their homes. Which is why the ultimate sacrifice made by a soldier demands the ultimate respect of the nation. On 26 June 2026, more than a year and a month after Operation Sindoor – the four-day military confrontation with Pakistan – the government of India revealed the names of six soldiers who were killed at the time in line of duty. Names of the six military personnel, Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Mood Muralinaik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh from the Army, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar from the Air Force, came to public knowledge when they were recently inscribed on a wall at the National War Memorial.
Delay in acknowledging military casualties does a great disservice to the families of the fallen soldiers. With their loved ones reduced to unsung statistics, families of the soldiers are often deprived of the honour that they rightfully deserve. The Indian defence apparatus’s tendency to conceal statistics in the name of national security raises an uncomfortable question: Does hiding the truth protect the country, or does it merely shield the government from accountability? Operation Sindoor was launched in May 2025 in retaliation for the Pahalgam terror attack of 22 April 2025, in which 26 civilians lost their lives. Terror infrastructure was targeted in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, and was followed by four days of military exchanges before both sides reached an understanding to end the hostilities. Admittedly, military operations mostly require a high level of secrecy. It is understood that tactical information, troop movements and operational details cannot be disclosed while the hostilities continue. But once operations conclude, the identities of the personnel killed in action should not remain in administrative limbo.
Historically, the sacrifice of our defenders has always met with public reverence and collective mourning. Today, however, the System increasingly chooses suppression over transparency. The social media is full of accusations that the government is deliberately concealing the details of casualties for a year and has misled even the Parliament. The country has observed the telecast showing the vehemence with which Defence Minister Rajnath Singh claimed in Parliament on 28 July 2025 that not a single Indian soldier was harmed during Operation Sindoor. Hiding facts from the public, it seems, has been ingrained in our system, irrespective of the political party in power.
Concealing facts, publishing lies and manipulating figures is a systemic issue in India for a long. A similar pattern was observed during the capture of Wing Commander Abhinandan Varthaman by Pakistan in 2019. When senior military officials claimed that all Indian aircraft and pilots had returned safely to base after conducting airstrikes in Balakot in February 2019, Pakistani social media showed the downing of a MiG 21 and capture of the pilot. If hiding facts is intended to boost the morale of the people, then getting caught later is even more demoralising. Similarly, during the Bahanaga triple train crash of June 2023, the railway authorities were seen spouting and manipulating the death toll. Those who cared had found out how all the morgues, starting from Balasore down the coastal belt of this state, were filled with crushed bodies for long, waiting for relatives to claim the remains. Many who could not be identified were cremated very unceremoniously.
Democracies earn credibility not by presenting casualty-free narratives during any military action or any event, for that matter, but by revealing the truth to the public so that lessons may be learned from mistakes. This malaise should therefore rise above partisan politics. Neither the ruling establishment nor the Opposition should reduce the sacrifice of soldiers to a political contest. The real focus must remain on ensuring that every fallen soldier receives timely and dignified recognition and the bereaved families get due recognition and compensation immediately, irrespective of the political party in power. The six names now engraved on the National War Memorial could have secured their rightful place in the nation’s his tory, albeit very late. But India owes its soldiers more than eventual remembrance on a flat wall surface. It owes them prompt acknowledgement, complete transparency and an unwavering commitment that no sacrifice in its defence will ever wait for inefficient defence official recognition.
A country that sleeps peacefully because its soldiers stand guard at the borders has the right to know who has fallen to keep it safe. True patriotism cannot be built on the foundation of falsehood.

Heading: PLA set up camps allegedly inside Taksing area | Terming ‘encroachment’, NWS seeks GoAP-GoI intervention | Arunachal Observer
Summary: A community organization, the NAH Welfare Society (NWS), alleges that the Chinese PLA has encroached upon Indian territory in Arunachal Pradesh's Taksing circle, establishing military camps and infrastructure in traditionally used areas. The NWS has sought urgent intervention from the state and central governments, expressing alarm over the alleged occupation and the perceived inadequacy of the current response. The article also references a hypothetical future military operation by India, warning China against further provocations and highlighting India's strong defense capabilities.
Content: By Special Correspondent ITANAGAR, June 28: A community organisation has alleged that Chinese People’s Liberation Army (PLA) has established military camps and infrastructure deep inside Indian territory in remote Taksing circle of Upper Subansiri district, raising fresh concerns over border encroachment along India-China frontier. The NAH Welfare Society (NWS), a registered organisation based in Taksing, has written to Upper Subansiri deputy commissioner, claiming that the PLA has occupied several areas traditionally used by local communities and built roads, bridges and military camps over the past five years. In a letter dated June 26, signed by NWS president Keru Chader, the NWS has identified five locations—Oying (2445) in Asaphila area, Paniar in Chujarta, Marpan (Marnafe), Potrang Lake and Tindingtang—as areas now allegedly under Chinese occupation. According to the NWS, these sites were “firmly within Indian territory” before 2020, with some of them holding religious significance as sacred pilgrimage sites in the Tsari region. “We are losing our land inch by inch day by day to them. The intention and speed of the present activities of the Chinese PLA at Taksing area is very alarming and a matter of grave concern for us,” Chader wrote in the letter. The NWS alleged that ancestral hunting grounds and traditional cattle-grazing areas, used freely by local residents for generations, have been taken over by Chinese forces. It further claimed that extensive military infrastructure, including well-connected roads and permanent camps, has come up in these areas in recent years. “The Chinese Govt is very fast expanding their territory by occupying new and important places of our land situated at border area,” the letter said and urged both the GoAP and the GoI to tackle the issue. While expressing faith in the Indian Army’s commitment to defending the border, the NWS said the current response has not been sufficient to halt the alleged encroachment. “They have been guarding our land for many years, but their efforts are not enough,” Chader wrote. Taksing, a strategically significant village in the Upper Subansiri district, is located approximately 7-km from international India-China border. The NWS has also enclosed photographs with the letter, claiming they show Chinese military activities in the disputed areas, and has sought immediate intervention from state and central authorities to safeguard the region’s territorial integrity. The allegations come amid continuing concerns over infrastructure expansion and territorial claims by China along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh, which Beijing claims as part of “South Tibet” despite India’s repeated rejection of such assertions.There has been no immediate response from the district administration, the Indian Army or the Ministry of External Affairs on the allegations made by the organisation. This sensitive state shares 1,129-km of total 3,488-km Indo-China border. But, Bejing should not forget Operation SINDOOR, launched on 07.05.25 by Indian Armed Forces in response to 22.04.25 Pahalgam terror massacre that claimed the lives of 26 civilians. Pakistan-backed attackers stormed a village, asked people their religion, and killed them, resulting in 26 deaths. A clear attempt to incite communal violence, this marked a shift, from cross-border attacks to dividing India from within. Pakistan armed with Chinese-made wherewithal had responded but India’s Integrated Counter UAS Grid and air defense systems successfully thwarted these offensives. Military actions ceased on 10.05.25 after the Directors General of Military Operations (DGMO) agreed to halt hostilities, but the ineffectiveness of China’s weapons was exposed. China should avoid misadventure in Indo-China border to provoke India to launch another operation ‘Demolish Han Ego’.

Heading: "They inscribed his name at War Memorial, want my children to follow his footsteps": Wife of Op Sindoor hero
Summary: The family of Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar Sharma expressed immense pride and gratitude after his name was inscribed at the National War Memorial for his sacrifice in Operation Sindoor. His wife thanked the government for the honour and support, while his mother urged the completion of local memorial work. Operation Sindoor, conducted in May 2025, successfully targeted terror leaders and avenged the Pahalgam terror attack, with Indian forces striking nine terror targets.
Content: Palwal (Haryana) [India], June 28 (ANI): Family members of Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar Sharma , one of the six bravehearts who laid down their lives during Operation Sindoor, on Sunday expressed gratitude after his name was inscribed at the National War Memorial in New Delhi, calling it a matter of immense pride and honour. Speaking to ANI, Sharma's wife, Seema Devi, said the recognition reflected the nation's respect for the sacrifices made by its soldiers and thanked the government for supporting the martyr's family. "This village, country, and I are proud of my husband for the sacrifice he did for the nation. I thank the government for bestowing such great honour upon us. They have inscribed his name at the War Memorial in Delhi and provided me with a job as a clerk in the Education Department. I want my children to follow his footsteps. CM Nayab Saini had visited when he was martyred," she said. His mother, Meera Devi, also welcomed the government's recognition but urged authorities to complete the pending memorial work in the village. "The government is honouring us, it is a matter of great pride. I feel very proud that my son brought honour to India. The Chief Minister had spoken about renaming the village, but the name hasn't been changed yet. That should happen. We have received all due recognition. However, the work on the statue and memorial hasn't been fully completed yet, and that needs to be finished. My child sacrificed his life for India, and he deserves to be honoured properly," she said. The names of the six Indian security personnel who died during the four-day armed operation against Pakistan in May 2025 have been etched at the National War Memorial in New Delhi. Operation Sindoor were carried out to avenge the victims of the Pahalgam terror attack and to eliminate Jaish-e-Mohammed (JeM) and Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) leaders involved in planning and executing terrorist attacks in India on May 2025. Indian Armed Forces successfully struck nine terror targets, four in Pakistan, including Bahawalpur, Muridke, and Sialkot, and five in Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoJK), using special precision munitions in a coordinated operation. The operation was jointly carried out by the Indian Army, Navy, and Air Force, with the mobilisation of assets and troops. (ANI) News

Heading: Military personnel death cover-up issue; Did Rajnath Singh mislead Parliament..? Opposition attacks Union Government
Summary: Opposition parties have accused Union Minister Rajnath Singh of misleading Parliament by allegedly concealing the deaths of six military personnel during 'Operation Sindoor' in 2024, whose names were recently inscribed at the National War Memorial. Congress leaders questioned the minister's awareness or honesty regarding the incident. The Ministry of Defense, however, clarified that the minister's statement was misrepresented and intended to refute rumors, adding that the sacrifices were previously acknowledged and awards presented.
Content:
New Delhi: Opposition parties have complained against Union Minister Rajnath Singh for allegedly providing false information in Parliament by concealing the deaths of military personnel during 'Operation Sindoor'. During 'Operation Sindoor' in 2024, a total of six personnel, five from the Indian Army and one from the Air Force, were martyred. Regarding this, during a debate in the Lok Sabha on July 28, 2025, Union Defense Minister Rajnath Singh had stated, 'No Indian soldiers were harmed during this operation.'

Now, the names of the martyred Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar (Vir Chakra), Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Aviation Technician Mood Murali Naik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh, and Air Force Sergeant Surendra Kumar (Vayu Medal) have been officially inscribed at the National War Memorial in Delhi. Following the release of the soldiers' names, the Congress party has strongly condemned Rajnath Singh for misleading Parliament. Commenting on this, Congress leaders Manish Tewari and Pawan Khera, in an interview, questioned, 'Does the Union Minister not know what is happening in his own ministry, or did he lie in Parliament by concealing the truth?'

In response, the Ministry of Defense has clarified, 'The Minister's statement is being misrepresented; he said so to refute rumors that pilots had died in Operation Sindoor. Furthermore, the Director General of Military Operations had already informed about the soldiers' sacrifice in a press conference. Awards for their heroic deeds were presented on August 14, 2025.'

Heading: Haryana's Dinesh, martyred in Operation Sindoor, named on War Memorial; 6 Indian soldiers made the supreme sacrifice
Summary: The Central Government has officially recognized six Indian soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor, including Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar from Haryana, by inscribing their names on the National War Memorial's Roll of Honour and 3D wall. This operation involved the Indian Army's retaliatory strikes on terrorist hideouts in PoK following a terrorist attack in Pahalgam, leading to the elimination of over 100 terrorists. The government has also provided extensive support to martyr Dinesh Kumar's family, including financial aid, a job for his wife, and naming local infrastructure in his honour.
Content:
Palwal (Dinesh Kumar): Six Indian soldiers were martyred in Operation Sindoor. The Central Government officially released their names. These names have been included in the Roll of Honour on the National War Memorial website. Their names have also been inscribed in the 2025 section on the 3D wall of the National War Memorial in New Delhi. The Tyag Chakra of the National War Memorial has 16 circular granite walls, on which the name, rank, and unit of every soldier who sacrificed their life for the country since independence are written.

Actually, on April 22, a terrorist attack took place in Pahalgam, Jammu and Kashmir, in which 26 tourists were killed. The Indian Army attacked terrorist hideouts in PoK on the night of May 6-7. During this, more than 100 terrorists were killed. An aerial war lasted for 4 days between India and Pakistan. A ceasefire was declared between the two countries on May 10.

Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, a resident of Mohammadpur village in Palwal district, Haryana, was posted in Poonch. In response to Pakistani shelling, he took charge with 4 comrades and was martyred in the counter-attack. Regarding the honour given to martyr Dinesh Kumar by the government, his wife Seema Devi said that she is proud of her husband's martyrdom, who sacrificed his life for the defense of the country. She said that the Central Government and the State Government have provided all possible assistance to the family members of martyr Dinesh Kumar. A martyr's memorial is being constructed in his honour. The village has been named after martyr Dinesh Kumar. The school and park have also been named after the martyr. Financial assistance has also been provided by the government. The martyr's wife has been given a job as a clerk in the Education Department, for which she expressed gratitude to the government.

Heading: Names of soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor revealed for the first time, know what the government said?
Summary: The Ministry of Defence has clarified a political controversy surrounding the identification of six soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor, refuting claims that their sacrifice was hidden or only recently recognized. The Ministry stated that these national heroes were promptly honored with tributes, gallantry awards, and their names inscribed on the National War Memorial following due protocol. It condemned misleading claims for causing distress and tarnishing the honor of the brave soldiers.
Content:
A political controversy has arisen regarding the identification of six soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor. The government has issued an official statement clarifying this controversy.
A political controversy has arisen regarding the identification of six soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor. The opposition claims that the government had hidden the martyrdom of soldiers during the operation against Pakistan. All six soldiers were identified after their names were inscribed on the National War Memorial. The government has issued an official statement clarifying this controversy, stating that all six brave soldiers are "heroes" of the nation and their courage, dedication, and supreme sacrifice will continue to inspire future generations.
According to the Ministry of Defence, misleading claims are being made on some media and social media platforms that the six brave soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice during Operation Sindoor were recently officially recognized or their sacrifice was revealed for the first time. According to the Ministry of Defence, this claim is completely factually incorrect.
The reality is that the nation had paid timely tribute to these heroes long before the news broke. The day after Operation Sindoor concluded, on May 11, 2025, in a joint press conference of the three armed forces, the then Director General of Military Operations (DGMO) Lieutenant General Rajiv Ghai paid heartfelt tribute to these brave soldiers and clearly stated that the soldiers had made the supreme sacrifice while on duty during Operation Sindoor.
Subsequently, these brave soldiers were honored with gallantry awards for their unparalleled courage and sacrifice. This official information was released through a press release issued on August 14, 2025. This honor, in keeping with the highest traditions of the Indian Armed Forces, is a formal and national recognition of their bravery, dedication, and supreme sacrifice.

Heading: Centre debunks social media claims over Rajnath Singh’s Operation Sindoor speech
Summary: The Union government rejected social media claims that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh denied Indian soldier casualties during Operation Sindoor, clarifying his remarks were taken out of context and specifically targeted false narratives about IAF pilot deaths. The Ministry of Defence highlighted the operation's success in precision strikes against terror infrastructure, resulting in significant enemy casualties and damage. The government reaffirmed its commitment to honoring fallen personnel, whose names are inscribed on the National War Memorial, and providing welfare benefits to their families.
Content:
The Union government on Saturday (June 27, 2026) rejected the “misleading social media claims” that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had stated that no Indian soldier was killed during Operation Sindoor, asserting that his remarks in Parliament had been selectively quoted and stripped of their context.

On July 28, 2025, while speaking before the Lok Sabha, Rajnath Singh clearly stated that no Indian soldiers were harmed during Operation Sindoor.

While speaking for 55 minutes during the 16-hour-long discussion, he said, “If you want to raise a question, then ask whether any of our brave soldiers were harmed in this operation. The answer is, no, none of our soldiers were harmed.”

 Congress accuses Rajnath Singh of misleading Parliament on Operation Sindoor casualties

“When the objectives are high then our attention should not be on irrelevant issues. Because by focusing on irrelevant issues at times, our attention gets diverted from important issues related to national security and morale of soldiers,” Mr. Singh said.

On multiple occasions, Army Chief General Upendra Dwivedi and Mr. Singh have both affirmed that the Operation Sindoor is ongoing. The pause is viewed not as permanent peace, but as a temporary cessation of hostilities while India keeps its forces on high alert.

The Ministry of Defence (MoD) clarified in a statement that certain social media posts had misrepresented the Defence Minister’s address in Parliament, by isolating a portion of his speech to falsely suggest that he denied any Indian military casualties during the cross-border operation.

 Why it took nearly a year for Operation Sindoor martyrs’ names to reach the National War Memorial

According to the clarification, Mr. Singh’s remarks were specifically intended to counter a widely circulated false narrative at the time claiming that Indian Air Force pilots had been killed during Operation Sindoor. The government said this misinformation was being actively amplified in sections of the media and on social media to undermine the operation’s success and weaken public morale.

“It was in direct reference to this specific and mischievous narrative that the Defence Minister made the statement in question,” the MoD said, adding that his remarks were a targeted response to false claims and not a denial of casualties suffered by the armed forces.

The statement emphasised that the Defence Minister’s address in Parliament highlighted the success of Operation Sindoor, during which Indian forces carried out precision strikes against terror infrastructure and military targets across the border. It said the operation resulted in the elimination of more than 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers, while inflicting significant damage on Pakistani air bases and military infrastructure along the Line of Control.

 Names of six personnel who died in action during Op Sindoor inscribed at National War Memorial

Reiterating the government’s commitment to honouring the armed forces, the statement said the nation holds the highest respect for personnel who laid down their lives in the line of duty. It noted that the names of those killed during Operation Sindoor have been inscribed on the National War Memorial in recognition of their supreme sacrifice.

 Armed forces ready for ‘Operation Sindoor 2.0’ if need arises, says Army chief

The government also said it has extended educational, healthcare and other welfare benefits to the families and dependents of the fallen personnel, reaffirming that their sacrifice would always be honoured with dignity and gratitude.

A day after the government officially disclosed the names of the military personnel who lost their lives during Operation Sindoor, the Congress on Saturday alleged that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh had misled Parliament by claiming that no Indian soldier was killed during the operation.

Heading: No delay in honouring Operation Sindoor heroes: Defence Ministry
Summary: The Defence Ministry clarified that there was no delay in honouring the six personnel killed during Operation Sindoor, refuting accusations of concealing their sacrifice. The ministry emphasized that their valor was acknowledged at the earliest opportunity, citing specific dates and events as proof.
Content:
Amid a political row over the six personnel killed during Operation Sindoor, the Defence Ministry said on Saturday that the nation had paid homage to them at the "earliest opportunity" and that their memory would always be honoured with dignity, gratitude and reverence. It said the fallen personnel had already been formally recognised through tributes, gallantry awards and ceremonial honours.

The statement came after the Congress accused the government of concealing the sacrifice of the six bravehearts for a year by not recognising their martyrdom. The ministry rejected that charge, saying reports and social media posts suggesting that their sacrifice had been acknowledged only recently were incorrect.

Without naming anyone, the ministry said "certain reports circulating in sections of the media and on social media platforms have incorrectly suggested that the supreme sacrifice of six bravehearts during Operation Sindoor have been acknowledged or brought to public notice for the first time only recently". It added, "It is clarified that the nation paid homage to these fallen heroes at the earliest opportunity, well before the reports in question."

The ministry said that during an official press conference on May 11, 2025, the then director general of military operations had paid solemn tribute to the soldiers and specifically acknowledged their sacrifice in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor. It also said the six personnel were "conferred with gallantry awards" and that this was published in a press release on August 14, 2025, constituting "a formal and national recognition of their valour and supreme sacrifice".

According to the ministry, the Indian Army's official social media platforms also carried tributes to the personnel "without delay". It added that during the Army Day Parade in Jaipur on January 15 this year, the Chief of the Army Staff presented the Sena Medal (Gallantry) to the families of three of the soldiers, while the Chief of the Air Staff did the same on October 8, 2025.

The ministry said, "The six bravehearts of Operation Sindoor are national heroes whose courage, devotion to duty and sacrifice will continue to inspire generations of Indians." It added that the Indian defence forces remain steadfast in honouring every soldier who has made the supreme sacrifice in defence of the nation.

The statement also referred to the inscription of the names of the six personnel on a wall at the National War Memorial as a tribute to the fallen heroes. The names, inscribed on wall number 3D of the Tyag Chakra, are Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar (VrC), Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Mood Muralinaik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh, and Indian Air Force Sergeant Surendra Kumar. The unit names of the personnel have also been inscribed.

Operation Sindoor was carried out to avenge the deadly Pahalgam terror attackon April 22 last year. On the inscription of names at the memorial, the ministry said the process was governed by an established and well-defined protocol, adding that the defence forces followed these procedures with due diligence, care and reverence in keeping with the solemnity of the honour being conferred.

The ministry's statement sought to make clear that the six personnel killed during Operation Sindoor had been publicly honoured through official tributes, awards, ceremonies and now their inscription at the National War Memorial.

Heading: Ministry of Defence responds to allegations of hiding martyrs' sacrifices, says respect was given at every level
Summary: The Ministry of Defence has responded to allegations by Congress regarding the non-recognition of six martyrs from Operation Sindoor, clarifying that these soldiers were honored promptly and their sacrifices publicly acknowledged. The ministry detailed various instances of recognition, including gallantry awards, inscriptions on the National War Memorial, and ceremonies by Army and Air Force chiefs. It condemned the controversy as distressing to the martyrs' families.
Content:
The Ministry of Defence has clarified on the Congress's allegation of not honoring the six martyrs of Operation Sindoor. The ministry said on Saturday that the country had honored these martyrs at the very first instance and their memory would always be remembered with respect and reverence.
This controversy began with an allegation by Congress leader Pawan Khera. Khera posted on social media on Friday and Saturday, stating that the government had hidden the sacrifice of six soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor for a year and did not grant them martyr status. He also shared a link to a news report on Friday.
In response to this allegation, the Ministry of Defence, without naming anyone, said that some media reports and social media posts incorrectly stated that the sacrifice of these six soldiers was recently brought to light for the first time.
The ministry clarified that the country had honored these martyrs much earlier. In a press conference held on May 11, 2025, the Director General Military Operations of the Army paid tribute to these soldiers and publicly acknowledged their sacrifice.
Subsequently, the announcement of gallantry awards for these soldiers was also published in a press release issued on August 14, 2025. They were also praised on the Army's social media page. This year, on January 15, during the Army Day Parade in Jaipur, the Army Chief presented Army Medals to the families of three soldiers. The Air Force Chief also presented this honor at a ceremony on October 8, 2025.
The ministry also stated that the names of these six soldiers have been inscribed on the wall of the National War Memorial. These include five Army personnel: Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Mood Muralinaik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh, and Air Force Sergeant Surendra Kumar. Operation Sindoor was launched last year to avenge the Pahalgam terrorist attack on April 22.
The ministry said that there is a fixed procedure for inscribing the names of martyrs on the memorial, which is followed with utmost care. The ministry called this controversy incorrect and regrettable, stating that it causes distress to the families of the martyrs.

Heading: Brief News (7)
Summary: The article presents several brief news items, including the Congress criticizing the central government over Operation Sindoor and the Ministry of Defense clarifying misleading social media posts. Content:
Delhi: The Congress criticized the central government for not mentioning the sacrifice of six Indian soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor in Parliament. The ministry said that these posts are propagating that the minister, in his speech in Parliament on July 28 last year, stated that no soldier died in Operation Sindoor.

Thiruvananthapuram: The 'Special Investigation Team' (SIT) interrogated Unnikrishnan Potty, the main accused in the Sabarimala temple gold theft case, for about eight hours. Official sources said on Saturday that it continued from Friday morning till night. The SIT will soon submit its final report to the court, and this interrogation is part of it. The SIT recently stated that the investigation into two cases regarding the reduction in the weight of gold foils affixed to the idol of the doorkeeper and the doors of the sanctum sanctorum has been completed, and a charge sheet will be filed soon. Potty was in charge of sending the gold foils to a Chennai-based company for plating.

Delhi: The NIA has filed a charge sheet against three more persons in the powerful bomb blast case involving a vehicle at the Red Fort in Delhi last year. Officials said on Saturday that these three include the absconding child specialist Dr. Muzaffar Ahmed (MBBS, MD), along with Jameer Ahmed Ahangir and Tufail Ahmed Bhat. Gifts officially received by government dignitaries from foreign governments and officials are stored in the Toshakhana.

This directive was issued by the Ministry of Civil Aviation at the request of the Union Health Ministry in view of the Ebola outbreak. Heading: Never hid information on Operation Sindoor deaths: Government
Summary: The defence ministry clarified that information about military personnel deaths during Operation Sindoor was never hidden, citing public announcements and gallantry awards. It rejected claims that the Defence Minister denied these deaths in Parliament, explaining his statement was a targeted response to false narratives about lost Indian pilots. The ministry asserted these misleading claims aimed to diminish the operation's success and demoralize public sentiment.
Content:
NEW DELHI: : The defence ministry Saturday asserted that information about the deaths of six military personnel during the May 7-10 2025
Operation Sindoor
was never hidden from the public, pointing out that in the press briefing held a day after operations were paused against Pakistan, the then Director General of Military Operations had mentioned the loss of the lives of the armed forces personnel and civilians.
“These bravehearts were conferred with gallantry awards and this was published in the press release of Aug 14, 2025,” the ministry said, while pointing out that “Army’s official social media platforms carried tributes to these bravehearts without delay”.
The ministry also rejected the claims circulating on social media and some media reports that defence minister Rajnath Singh, in his July 28 statement in Parliament, denied deaths of members of the services during military conflict with Pakistan.
“These (posts) are deliberately misleading and factually incorrect,” it said.
“Those who have sought to construct a controversy out of Raksha Mantri’s parliamentary address have done so by deliberately ignoring the full context of his remarks. It must be recalled that at the time of the address, a particularly persistent and dominant narrative had taken hold, both in certain sections of the media and on social media, which claimed Indian pilots had been lost during Op Sindoor.
This narrative was false, yet it was being amplified aggressively with the clear intent of diminishing the success of the operation and demoralising public sentiment.
“It was in direct reference to this specific and mischievous narrative that the Raksha Mantri made the statement in question. His remarks were, therefore, a targeted and contextually specific response to a falsehood that was gaining dangerous traction at that moment,” the ministry stated.

Heading: Names of Operation Sindoor martyrs concealed for 14 months, says Cong
Summary: The Congress party accused the Modi government of concealing the names of Operation Sindoor martyrs for 14 months, denying them due honor and transparency. Content: Claiming that the truth had finally come out, Congress leader and Colonel Rohit Chaudhry (retd) said the party had continuously raised its voice to honour the martyrs, organised Jai Hind Sabhas across the country and fought for justice for the families of the fallen soldiers. “The Modi government kept the names of Operation Sindoor martyrs hidden from the country for 14 months,” Chaudhry said, adding that the Army had also confirmed their martyrdom. Congress MP Randeep Singh Surjewala also targeted the government over the issue. “The age of a lie is short, the truth of martyrdom is indelible. What respect will people, who do not speak the truth even for martyrdom, show to the martyrs? Who will believe people who shamelessly lie in the temple of democracy,” asked Surjewala. Congress leader Pawan Khera also joined the attack, saying there could only be two explanations for the discrepancy -- The Defence Minister was unaware that six soldiers had been killed when he addressed Parliament, which raises serious questions about his understanding of the ministry, or he was aware of the facts and chose to conceal them. “The fact remains that our six soldiers made the supreme sacrifice in the line of duty, but their sacrifice was concealed. They were denied the honour and recognition that they deserved. Their families were robbed of the transparency they had the right to expect. This is an insult to our soldiers. No true patriot can remain silent or complacent about it,” Khera wrote on X. Rejecting the allegations, the Ministry of Defence has said that posts circulating on social media had sought to misrepresent Rajnath Singh’s address in Parliament on July 28, 2025, by falsely suggesting that he had claimed that no Indian soldier had lost his life during Operation Sindoor. The ministry said the Defence Minister’s remarks were made in response to a “persistent and dominant narrative” claiming that Indian pilots had been lost during Operation Sindoor, a claim it described as entirely false. “It was in direct reference to this specific and mischievous narrative that the Defence Minister made the statement in question,” it said, adding that his remarks were a context-specific response and not a denial of casualties suffered by the Indian forces during the operation. The ministry further said the government remained committed to honouring every member of the armed forces, especially those who have laid down their lives in the service of the nation, adding that their names had been inscribed on the walls of the National War Memorial and benefits had been extended to their families.

Heading: Centre refutes Opposition's claim that Rajnath misled Parl on Operation Sindoor casualties: 'Deliberately misleading...'
Summary: The Centre has refuted the Opposition's claim that Defence Minister Rajnath Singh misled Parliament regarding casualties in Operation Sindoor, clarifying his statement was aimed at countering false narratives about Indian Air Force pilot losses. The Defence Ministry emphasized that Singh's address was a proud and accurate account of the operation's success, which neutralized over 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers and caused significant damage to Pakistani military infrastructure. The government also disclosed the names of six personnel who died during the operation and confirmed welfare benefits for their families.
Content:
A day after the government released the names of six soldiers who lost their lives during Operation Sindoor last year, the Centre on Saturday rejected the opposition's allegation that defence minister Rajnath Singh had informed Parliament in July last year that the security forces had suffered no casualties.
In a statement, the defence ministry saidRajnath Singh's address was intended to counter the prevailing narrative that Indian Air Force pilots had been killed during Operation Sindoor.
“Certain posts circulating on social media platforms have sought to misrepresent the Raksha Mantri's address delivered on the floor of Parliament on July 28, 2025. These posts have selectively quoted an isolated portion of the speech to falsely imply that the Raksha Mantri claimed that no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor. These are deliberately misleading and factually incorrect,” the statement read.
“Those who have sought to construct a controversy out of Raksha Mantri's Parliamentary address have done so by deliberately ignoring the full context of his remarks. It must be recalled that at the time of the Raksha Mantri's address, a particularly persistent and dominant narrative had taken hold, both in certain sections of the media and on social media, which claimed that Indian pilots had been lost during Operation Sindoor. This narrative was entirely false, yet it was being amplified aggressively with the clear intent of diminishing the success of the operation and demoralising public sentiment. It was in direct reference to this specific and mischievous narrative that the Raksha Mantri made the statement in question. His remarks were, therefore, a targeted and contextually specific response to a falsehood that was gaining dangerous traction at that moment,” it added.
The ministry added that Rajnath Singh’s statement in Parliament was, in its entirety, “a proud and accurate account” of the success of Operation Sindoor, during which the Indian Armed Forces demonstrated “unmatched precision, resolve and military professionalism”.
“During the operation, more than 100 terrorists and Pakistani soldiers were neutralised, while Pakistani air bases and military deployments along the Line of Control suffered extensive and significant infrastructure damage. The address was a fitting tribute to the courage and capability of the Indian Defence Forces, and a clear message to those who wish India harm,” it said.
The government's statement follows allegations by the Opposition that Rajnath Singh had misled Parliament through his earlier remarks.
On Friday, the Centre disclosed thenames of six personnelwho were killed in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor: Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Murali Naik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh and Indian Air Force Sergeant Surendra Kumar.
Their names will be added to the National War Memorial in New Delhi.
The government also said it has ensured educational, healthcare and other welfare benefits for the families and dependents of the deceased personnel.

Heading: Congress alleges concealment of soldiers' martyrdom in 'Operation Sindoor'
Summary: The Congress party has accused the Indian government of insulting soldiers and misleading Parliament by concealing the martyrdom of six personnel during 'Operation Sindoor'. Content:

Pawan Khera, head of the party's media department, shared a video on 'X' of a part of Defense Minister Rajnath Singh's speech given in the Lok Sabha during last year's monsoon session, in which Singh can be heard saying that no harm was caused to the brave soldiers of the country during 'Operation Sindoor'.
In fact, the names of six military personnel who attained martyrdom while performing their duty during 'Operation Sindoor' last year have been inscribed on the National War Memorial. This is the first time the government has released the names of these six personnel after the military operation carried out by the Indian Armed Forces in May 2025.
