If so, it raises serious questions about a minister who is not aware of the affairs of the ministry he is leading." He added that the second possibility is that Singh knew the truth and yet chose to mislead Parliament.
According to Khera, this is even more serious, as it proves that this government lies to the country in the temple of democracy, under oath. The Congress leader said, "Whatever the truth, some facts do not change. Our six brave jawans made the supreme sacrifice while performing their duty. But their sacrifice was hidden. They were not given the honor and recognition they deserved. And their families were also deprived of the transparency they expected."
The Congress leader said, "This is an insult to our soldiers and no true patriot can remain silent or satisfied with this." Last year, after the terrorist attack in Pahalgam on April 22, the Indian Army launched fierce attacks on terrorist hideouts in Pakistan under 'Operation Sindoor'. The names of the six military personnel inscribed on wall number '3D' of the 'Tyag Chakra' at the National War Memorial include Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer M Muralinaik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh from the Army, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar from the Indian Air Force.

Heading: Weekly Defence Dispatch: Pakistan's Rafale kill claims collapse, Su-30MKI gets BrahMos fangs, Netra clears FOC and more
Summary: This weekly defence dispatch highlights India's accelerating military modernization, including the debunking of Pakistan's Rafale kill claims and the operational clearance of the indigenous Netra AEW&C system. It also covers the integration of BrahMos missiles on Su-30MKIs, early talks for defence exports to the UAE, the establishment of regional defence manufacturing clusters, and India's commitment to a debris-free space by 2030. The article underscores India's growing self-reliance and strategic partnerships in defence.
Content:
As India’s military modernisation accelerates on multiple fronts, Firstpost tracks the week’s key developments — IAF paperwork that quietly settled Pakistan’s Rafale kill claims, 40 BrahMos-armed Su-30MKIs with a combat track record from Operation Sindoor, the Netra AEW&C system receiving its long-awaited Final Operational Clearance, a US support package keeping Apache helicopters and M777 howitzers combat-ready, early talks for a UAE sale of BrahMos and Akashteer, seven regional defence manufacturing clusters anchored by IIT partnerships, and an Indian Navy visit to Vietnam that means more than it looks.
Pakistan’s claims that India lost Rafale jets during Operation Sindoor in May 2025 just took another hit. IAF paperwork shows all 36 Rafales bought under the 2016 France deal are still operational and flying.
Air Headquarters has sent RFPs to Dassault Aviation and Safran Aircraft Engines for a five-month bridge support package to keep the entire Rafale fleet running past September 18, 2026, according to Firstpost sources .
It’s worth remembering how specific Pakistan’s original claim was. Pakistan’s Air Vice Marshal Aurangzeb Ahmed said three Rafales were among the five aircraft downed, and provided electronic signatures of the jets along with the exact locations where they were hit. He didn’t stop at hardware and coordinates, he played audio, too: Ahmed told reporters he had an audio recording from the Rafale formation, saying “the call sign is Godzilla… those animals are extinct, so this one also got extinct,” before adding that “India had said they would have Rafales, and that’s why this time we targeted their centre of gravity in the shape of Rafales," and that Pakistan could have downed more but “showed restraint”. It was theatre delivered with total confidence, precise hardware, precise coordinates, and a one-liner built for clips.
And yet tail numbers Pakistan claimed were destroyed have since turned up flying again, including at the Republic Day parade in January, meaning India’s own flypasts were quietly disproving Islamabad’s “evidence” months before this tender ever surfaced.
You can also watch a detailed report by Firstpost here .
Bottom line : This isn’t a one-off. After the 2019 Balakot strike, Pakistan’s military spokesperson said Indian jets had “released payload in haste while escaping” near Balakot, causing “no casualties or damage,” with locals telling reporters “no one died, only some pine trees died, they were cut down, a crow also died”. This line that outlived the actual debate over what India’s strike hit. Go back further and Pakistan disowned its own regular soldiers during the Kargil War, refusing to accept their bodies to maintain the fiction that the intrusion was the work of irregulars, not its army, as it failed to hold any of the territory it had intruded. And in 1971, despite roughly 93,000 Pakistani servicemen surrendering in Dhaka, the largest capitulation since World War II, the loss has never been squarely owned in Pakistan’s domestic telling. Confident claims, precise-sounding detail, and a story that survives well past the moment the facts catch up, Rafale is just the latest chapter in a pattern that goes back over five decades.
India and the United Arab Emirates are in early discussions over the possible sale of two of India’s most prominent defence exports, the BrahMos supersonic cruise missile and the Akashteer air defence command-and-control system, according to a report by Firstpost .
The talks come amid growing interest in air and missile defence across the Gulf following months of regional instability and repeated drone and missile attacks.
Akashteer is among India’s newest indigenous battlefield networks. Developed by Bharat Electronics and the Army, it links radars, sensors and weapon systems into a single automated air defence grid.
BrahMos remains the flagship of India’s defence export push. The missile can be launched from land, sea and air platforms and has already been exported to the Philippines.
Why it matters : The interest in Akashteer is as significant as the interest in BrahMos. Until recently, Indian defence exports were largely platforms and munitions. Akashteer represents something different: a battlefield management system designed to connect sensors, shooters and commanders into a single network. If exported, it would signal growing confidence in India’s ability to supply not just weapons, but the digital architecture that modern militaries increasingly depend on.
A UAE deal would also extend India’s defence footprint deeper into the Gulf. The Philippines has already inducted BrahMos, while Vietnam and Indonesia remain in discussions. Abu Dhabi’s interest suggests Indian systems are now attracting attention well beyond South and Southeast Asia.
Around 40 IAF Su-30MKI fighters now carry the air-launched BrahMos, and more jets are still being added. The Su-30MKI is built in India under Russian license by HAL, and the IAF flies around 270 of these jets in total. The air-launched BrahMos is lighter than the land-based version and getting it onto the Su-30MKI took years of structural changes to the jet. Its current range is around 450 km, with plans to push that to 800 km. The trials for this are expected later this year.
Separately, Russia and India are working on hypersonic follow-ons to BrahMos, with NPO Mashinostroyenia’s chief designer Aleksandr Leonov involved on the Russian side. You can watch this video to learn more about this development.
A smaller BrahMos-NG is also coming, targeted for 2028-29, meant to fit lighter aircraft like Tejas and Rafale and eventually the AMCA. Around 84 more Su-30MKIs are due for the Super Sukhoi upgrade too, swapping in more indigenous avionics and radar as part of the wider self-reliance push in defence manufacturing.
Why it matters : Forty BrahMos-armed Su-30MKIs is operationally significant on its own. But the calculus shifts when you factor in that BrahMos has been fired in actual combat. That changes how adversaries have to think about the IAF’s reach. An 800 km-range variant clears most of Pakistan and reaches deep into western China from standoff distances that deny effective intercept windows. BrahMos-NG then extends that threat down to Tejas and Rafale, two far more numerous and cheaper-to-sortie platforms, multiplying the number of launch points without multiplying cost.
DRDO is upgrading the Archer-NG drone, once just a surveillance platform, into a full combat UAV that can hit both ground and air targets using Indian-made weapons. The drone was originally built for intelligence, surveillance, reconnaissance work, and that’s still part of the plan. It’s getting better sensors, radar, and secure comms for real time battlefield feeds. The expected endurance is over 18 hours, flying above 30,000 feet, so it can handle border watch and maritime patrols.
But the real story now is weapons. Archer-NG is being fitted to carry precision guided bombs, anti-tank missiles, and air-to-air weapons, including the Astra Mk-1, which would let it shoot down enemy jets, choppers, or drones up to 110 km away. Smart Anti-Airfield Weapons and laser guided bombs are also planned for ground strikes.
There’s AI built in too, for target recognition and swarming, so it can work alongside fighter jets and other drones.
Why it matters : Most Indian drones so far have stuck to surveillance. This one’s meant to do both, watch and strike in the same airframe, which puts it somewhere between a recon drone and a fighter jet. It also carries an AESA radar for tracking multiple targets at once and resisting jamming, plus a 300 kg payload.
DRDO’s Aeronautical Development Establishment is running the program with Bharat Electronics. Trials go on through 2027-28, surveillance version first, armed version after.
Bottom line : India’s exported missiles and platforms before. A drone that does ISR and strike together, built at home, would be something new for DRDO’s self-reliance push.
The Ministry of Defence is setting up seven regional defence manufacturing clusters across India, each with a lead state, co-lead states, and IIT partners. Defence Production Secretary Sanjeev Kumar has already held two stakeholder meetings and all seven clusters have been assigned themes and asked to submit roadmaps by next month.
The clusters are separate from the existing defence industrial corridors in Uttar Pradesh and Tamil Nadu. Karnataka leads the first, focused on policy and governance, with IISc Bengaluru and IIT Dharwad as partners. Maharashtra leads the second, covering indigenisation, startups, and MSMEs, backed by IIT Bombay. UP heads the third on testing and certification. Assam leads a dedicated northeastern cluster covering border states from Tripura to Ladakh. Telangana leads one on defence exports and market access. Gujarat heads a skill development and research cluster. Tamil Nadu leads the seventh on defence industrial infrastructure.
You can read more about it here .
Why it matters : India spent decades buying weapons it could have built. That is now changing, slowly but with more structure than before. Defence production hit Rs 1.78 lakh crore in FY26 — more than double what it was five years ago. Exports have crossed Rs 38,000 crore. But the gap between production numbers and real industrial depth is still wide. Most of what India produces still comes from government-owned firms. Private companies, startups, and MSMEs do not have the testing infrastructure, certification access, or market visibility to scale.
That is what these clusters are trying to fix. Putting IITs inside the manufacturing ecosystem, not just as universities but as testing and certification partners, is the kind of structural move that could actually move smaller firms up the value chain. If Viksit Bharat by 2047 means anything in defence terms, it means India designing, building, testing, and exporting its own weapons, not assembling foreign parts under licence. These clusters are an early attempt to build the ground for that.
India’s homegrown eye in the sky just got its full stamp of approval, years after it had already been flying real missions. On June 25 in Bengaluru, the IAF formally received Final Operational Clearance for Netra, the indigenous radar-and-command jet that spots threats early and directs fighters to intercept them. The twist is that the IAF trusted Netra enough to induct it operationally even before this final clearance came through, and it saw real combat use in the Balakot strikes and Operation Sindoor as reported by News18. Initial clearance came in 2017, but the programme itself traces back to 2004, making this the payoff of a two-decade effort. India fielded this in actual combat before the paperwork caught up, a rare reversal in defence procurement, where certification usually comes long before trust.
Why it matters : AEW&C aircraft extend a force’s vision deep into enemy airspace, tracking aircraft and missiles before they show up on ground radar and feeding that picture to fighters and air defences in real time. India has relied on Israel’s Phalcon system for this role. A fully cleared indigenous alternative reduces that dependence.
With Pakistan and China both expanding their own airborne early warning fleets, having a domestic system that’s already proven itself in Sindoor and Balakot, rather than just on paper, strengthens India’s hand both operationally and as a credible option to eventually offer to other countries shopping for the same capability.
#WATCH | Jaisalmer, Rajasthan | The Indian Army showcased the firepower and advanced combat capabilities of its Apache attack helicopters during Exercise Brahmastra at the Pokhran Firing Range. Also called the ‘tanks in the air’, the advanced helicopters showcased… pic.twitter.com/bFBKpPcS80
Last week Washington quietly dropped ‘Indo’ from Indo-Pacific Command, reverting to the old US Pacific Command name, a symbolic snub that had New Delhi wondering if India was being nudged out of the picture. This week, the same Washington wired through a $482.2 million support package for India’s Apache helicopters and M777 howitzers. About $230 million of it covers spare parts, training and repairs for the M777 howitzers, with the remaining $198.2 million going toward sustainment for the AH-64E Apaches. Including engineering support, technical publications, training, and all that keeps hardware combat-ready. Washington, as reported by Firstpost , was upfront about its own stake too: the deal is framed as serving America’s foreign policy and national security goals while strengthening India’s capability to deter regional threats. The IAF flies 22 Apaches and the Army six; the Army’s 145 M777s, 120 of them assembled locally by Mahindra, round out the fleet.
Why it matters : Mixed signals or just business as usual? Probably the latter, names are cheap, parts and ammunition aren’t. The Apache is India’s only helicopter that can hunt tanks at night, at altitude, from standoff range. The M777 is light enough to be airlifted into terrain nothing else can reach, and it proved that during Operation Sindoor. Neither has an Indian-made substitute waiting in the wings, so keeping both fed with spares and training isn’t routine procurement, it’s what keeps the doctrine working. Whatever the nameplate on a Hawaii command center says, the supply chain underneath it just got a very practical vote of confidence.
A new analysis from LeoLabs lays out just how much space junk China is leaving behind. Between January 2021 and January 2025, China abandoned 51 spent rocket bodies in low Earth orbit above 650 km. That’s 86 percent of everything left behind globally. For some perspective: the US left behind four over that stretch, Russia just one. The total mass of rocket bodies China has left behind in space has more than tripled over the years. Three of these rocket bodies have already exploded in the past four years, and debris from blasts like that can stay up there for decades posing a threat to the space assets of other countries.
Why it matters : India has dozens of operational satellites in low earth orbit. Many are crucial for military communication, earth observation etc. According to ISRO’s Space Situational Awareness reports, Indian satellites have to perform dozens of collision avoidance manoeuvres to dodge incoming space junk.
There’s actually a rulebook for managing space junk that more than 60 countries have signed. China is a signatory but has paid scant regard to the rules. On the other hand, India has shown exemplary foresight in managing this problem. Under its Debris Free Space Mission initiative, ISRO has committed to achieving zero debris creation by 2030. ISRO has institutionalised a process where launch vehicles are designed to de-orbit and burn up in the atmosphere.
Taiwan is on a five day military drill from June 22. Tanks and armoured vehicles from the Army’s 269th Infantry Brigade were seen rolling through city streets in Taoyuan, home to the island’s main international airport. The drills are built to test how fast units can mobilise if Chinese pressure suddenly tips into something more dangerous. China has been employing what is called as grey-zone tactics, aggressive drone flights and naval patrols in the Taiwanese airspace and nearby to test the country’s defences. Earlier this month Taiwan fired rockets toward China for the first time in an exercise.
This drill comes at a time when China has spent the past few weeks running coastguard patrols east of Taiwan. Beijing has dismissed criticism from the US, Britain, France and Germany over these deployments. Meanwhile, walking back on the doubts US President Donal Trump has created over continued US support to Taipei, a senior US diplomat has told the US Congress that Washington still stands by its decades-old “Six Assurances” to Taiwan. But reassurances only go so far. The same Trump administration has set no timeline for releasing a stalled $14 billion arms package for Taiwan. Even if Washington wanted to move faster on this, the its doubtful if the US industrial base can produce enough weapons fast enough to transport to Taiwan in case of a conflict.
Why it matters : Taiwan runs readiness drills often, but staging tanks through a city next to the island’s main international airport is a visible signal, to its own public and to Beijing, that rapid mobilisation is the priority right now, not deterrence on paper. That signal lands at a moment when China is testing the waters with coastguard patrols Beijing won’t back down from, and the US is reaffirming old promises without backing them with new arms or a fast enough supply chain to make good on them if things actually escalate. Delhi will be watching the developments keenly, as any threat to Taiwan is a direct threat to India’s supply lines to semiconductors.
The British Army is sending around 350 troops from the Parachute Regiment to a training ground in Alberta, Canada for an exercise called Rhino Biz this July. The focus is on testing the unmanned and counter-drone kit both UK and Canadian armies actually need, and employing them effectively. A number of drone and counter-drone firms are joining in for the exercise. The Canadian Army’s chief Lieutenant-General Michael Wright has said that they aee also rolling out a 22-day course called the Soldier First Course. The idea is to make every recruit adept at operating a drone or defending against one.
INS Udaygiri and INS Kavaratti reached Ho Chi Minh City on June 22. Both the ships are in Vietnam as part of an Eastern Fleet deployment to Southeast Asia, the two navies will hold officer meetings, cross-deck visits, sports, and community activities.
Why it matters : In May 2026, India and Vietnam upgraded their relationship to an Enhanced Comprehensive Strategic Partnership , as reported by Firstpost. A warship visit within weeks is New Delhi putting that on paper into practice. Vietnam has had its own disputes with China over the South China Sea for decades. China, meanwhile, has naval access points in Pakistan, Sri Lanka, and Myanmar — all close to India. The two countries have more reason than most to keep each other close, and this visit reflects that.
The Army and ITBP finished up a joint training programme and coordination conference in Arunachal Pradesh on June 24, meant to tighten up how the two forces work together along the border. Defence PRO Lt Col Mahendra Rawat said it covered tactical coordination in the state’s high-altitude terrain, with troops running through mountain warfare drills, route familiarisation, comms procedures, casualty evacuation, and practising joint responses.
Why it matters : Arunachal sits right against the LAC, and this kind of Army-ITBP coordination isn’t new, but how often these drills are happening this year says something about how seriously both forces are taking joint readiness in that sector right now.

Heading: There was happiness at home from the last posting, but he returned as a martyr: The story of brave Subedar Major Pawan Kumar of Operation Sindoor
Summary: The article recounts the story of Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, one of six martyrs from 'Operation Sindoor', whose names were recently made public and inscribed in the National War Memorial. Content:
Subedar Major Pawan Kumar was among the six martyrs who were martyred during Operation Sindoor. For the first time on Friday, the army has made public the names of these six martyrs and given them a place in the National War Memorial.
Our mornings used to start with reading Dad's good morning messages. That day, when the message didn't come, we felt uneasy. Before we could think anything, a senior army officer called and delivered the most tragic news of our lives. He informed us that our father had been martyred in the ongoing conflict with Pakistan. This is the story of Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, who was martyred on the Punjab border during Operation Sindoor. He was martyred last year in May during Operation Sindoor, but now his name has also been included in the National War Memorial in Delhi.
He was martyred in Pakistani firing. 50-year-old Subedar Major Pawan Kumar Jaryal was due to retire on August 31 last year. He had taken his last posting near his home in Punjab, and preparations for his return were underway at home three months later. Major Pawan Kumar's father had also served in the army. His father, Garaj Singh Jaryal, said that he would have retired in the next three months, and preparations for his welcome were on. Who knew that he would not return now, and only his body, wrapped in the tricolor, would come home.
Pawan Kumar's father, Garaj Singh Jaryal, says that his son would have been nearby three months later. He had served in the army for 32 years. It was just a matter of a few months; we were all very happy. But who would have thought that he would return home wrapped in the tricolor? After tensions flared between India and Pakistan, I was only able to talk to him once. He had told me that they were all hiding in bunkers.
Retired Havildar Garaj Singh could not hold back his tears while narrating this. Besides Pawan Kumar's parents, he is survived by his wife Sushma Devi and two children. Son Abhishek is 22 years old, and daughter Anamika is 21 years old. Abhishek is studying in Dharamshala from IGNOU Study Center. Abhishek said that they were happy with his father's daily messages. That day, a message came that his father had suffered a deep head injury. Then another call came saying that he had been martyred.
The names of the six soldiers who lost their lives during 'Operation Sindoor' are inscribed on the 'Tyag Chakra'. These include five soldiers from the Indian Army and one Air Warrior from the Indian Air Force. Among them are Rifleman Sunil Kumar, honored with the Vir Chakra, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar, who received the Air Force Medal; both were posthumously honored for their bravery.
'Operation Sindoor' was launched last year in May in response to the deadly terrorist attack in Pahalgam, which claimed the lives of 26 civilians. The Indian armed forces carried out precise strikes on terrorist bases across the border, but these six brave soldiers also lost their lives in this operation.
Now their names are recorded alongside thousands of other soldiers who made the supreme sacrifice for the country. For their families, having their names inscribed is not just a matter of honor. It is a lasting memory that tells them the country has not forgotten their loved ones. Every person visiting the National War Memorial will now pass by these names; each name tells a story of courage, duty, and sacrifice.

Heading: What is Tyag Chakra, where the names of 6 martyrs of Operation Sindoor will be inscribed
Summary: The article details 'Tyag Chakra' at the National War Memorial in Delhi, where the names of 6 Indian soldiers martyred in 'Operation Sindoor' will be inscribed. Inspired by the Mahabharata's Chakravyuh, this monument honors over 25,000 martyrs from various wars, aiming to instill nationalism and patriotism in current and future generations. It also briefly describes the other three chakras: Amar Chakra, Veerta Chakra, and Rakshak Chakra, each symbolizing different aspects of India's defense and valor.
Content:
Circle of Sacrifice In Delhi: The names of 6 Indian soldiers martyred during 'Operation Sindoor' will be inscribed in 'Tyag Chakra'. In such a situation, it is also important to know what this Tyag Chakra is and when it was built.
The Government of India has officially made public for the first time the names of 6 Indian soldiers martyred in 'Operation Sindoor', launched by India against terrorism. Five of them were Army personnel and one was Air Force personnel. These brave soldiers of the Indian Army have been registered on the National War Memorial's website 'Roll of Honour'. Their names will also be inscribed in golden letters in Delhi's 'Tyag Chakra'. This information has been provided by the National War Memorial. In such a situation, it also becomes important to know what 'Tyag Chakra' located in Delhi is and when it was built.
Tyag Chakra is one of the four major concentric circles built in the National War Memorial complex near India Gate in New Delhi. Tyag Chakra has been built for the brave martyrs of the Indian Armed Forces who made the supreme sacrifice while defending the country. Through this chakra, these brave soldiers have been immortalized forever. Because India has fought many major wars since independence. Many military operations have also been carried out, in which thousands of soldiers have sacrificed their lives for their motherland. Their names are inscribed in the Tyag Chakra. The walls of Tyag Chakra are made of granite stones.
Tyag Chakra is inspired by the Chakravyuh pattern of Mahabharata. It has 16 circular walls made of granite stones, with the names of more than 25,000 martyrs inscribed in golden letters. The nation will always be indebted to these brave soldiers. The names of martyrs from the 1962 India-China War, 1965 India-Pakistan War, 1971 India-Pakistan War, and 1999 India-Pakistan Kargil War are inscribed in Tyag Chakra. This chakra reminds citizens who visit here of the selfless sacrifice of many heroes hidden in the defense of India. The names of the 6 soldiers martyred in Operation Sindoor will also be inscribed in golden letters in this Tyag Chakra. A major objective of this chakra is also to convey the spirit of nationalism, patriotism, and dutifulness to the present and future generations.
There is also an important reason for taking the structure of Tyag Chakra from Chakravyuh. Because this structure tells about the courage of the soldiers as well as their strategy on how to always stand firm on the battlefield. In such a situation, when common people of the country come to Tyag Chakra and see the names of these brave soldiers, a sense of respect for the nation and passion for the country arises in their minds. This chakra creates a sense of unity among Indians.
Besides this, there are three other chakras here. These include 'Amar Chakra'. This monument is the central and inner circle, which is considered a symbol of the immortality of martyrs. Here stands a 15.2-meter-high giant granite pillar, in which the 'Amar Jawan Jyoti' burns 24 hours a day. This sacred flame tells the people of the country about the never-ending spirit and immortal contribution of those who defended the country.
Veerta Chakra is the second chakra built in the National War Memorial. It has been built as a covered gallery. On its walls are depicted scenes from the six most famous and historic wars fought by the Indian Armed Forces, including the Army, Navy, and Air Force. Seeing these pictures gives you an introduction to the courage of the Indian Army. These pictures bring that scene to life. This chakra sings the saga of the combat skills of the Indian Army.
The fourth chakra is 'Rakshak Chakra'. It is considered a symbol of the unbreakable security of India's borders. This chakra is made of more than 600 dense trees planted in a row. This row indicates that just as these trees surround the memorial, our country's soldiers surround our borders. Here, brave Indian soldiers protect the country day and night.

Future generations will know how Subedar Pawan Kumar displayed extraordinary courage and devotion to duty, making the supreme sacrifice for the country. Summary: The names of six Indian soldiers killed during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, a military clash with Pakistan, have been inscribed on the National War Memorial. These soldiers, including recipients of gallantry awards, were part of an operation that saw India strike terror and military targets in Pakistan and PoK, leading to Pakistan's surrender. The operation was a response to the Pahalgam terror strike and involved extensive air and ground strikes.
Content:
NEW DELHI: The names of six Indian soldiers killed in action in May 2025 during Operation Sindoor, the four-day military clash with Pakistan, were inscribed on the National War Memorial in Delhi, officials aware of the matter said on Friday.

The casualties included five men from the army and one from the Indian Air Force. Two of them were posthumously decorated with gallantry awards last year for their heroism: Rifleman Sunil Kumar (Vir Chakra) and Sergeant Surendra Kumar (Vayu Sena Medal). Sunil Kumar was from 4 Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry, while Surendra Kumar was a medical assistant posted with 39 Wing at Udhampur .

The names and units disclosed for the first time are Subedar Major Pawan Kumar (HQ 10 Infantry Brigade; died on May 10, 2025), Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar (5 Field Regiment; died on May 7, 2025), AV Mood Muralinaik (851 Light Regiment; died on May 9, 2025) and Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh (237 Field Workshop Company; died on June 6, 2025).

The soldiers were posted at frontline bases during the operation. However, the sequence of events leading to their deaths wasn’t immediately known.

In May 2025, the army revealed it had lost five soldiers during Operation Sindoor.

On August 14, 2025, India acknowledged the heroism of its soldiers who took part in the operation, playing a pivotal role in hitting terror and military targets in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir; President Droupadi Murmu then approved scores of wartime honours for them.

Among the 127 gallantry medals and 40 distinguished service awards cleared by the President on the eve of the 79th Independence Day were four Kirti Chakras, 15 Vir Chakras, 16 Shaurya Chakras, two Bar to Sena Medals (Gallantry), 58 Sena Medals (Gallantry), six Nao Sena Medals (Gallantry), 26 Vayu Sena Medals (Gallantry), seven Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medals, nine Uttam Yudh Seva Medals and 24 Yudh Seva Medals.

The Vir Chakra awardees included Colonel Koshank Lamba, Lieutenant Colonel Sushil Bisht, Naib Subedar Satish Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Group Captain Ranjeet Singh Sidhu, Group Captain Manish Arora, Group Captain Animesh Patni, Group Captain Kunal Kalra, Wing Commander Joy Chandra, Squadron Leader Sarthak Kumar, Squadron Leader Siddhant Singh, Squadron Leader Rizwan Malik, Flight Lieutenant Aarshveer Singh, BSF Sub Inspector Mohd Imteyaz (Posthumous) and Constable Deeapk Chingakham (Posthumous).

India launched Operation Sindoor in the early hours of May 7, 2025, striking terror and military installations in Pakistan and PoK following the Pahalgam terror strike that killed 26 people.

Between the launch of the operation in the early hours of May 7 and the ceasefire on the evening of May 10, Indian forces bombed nine terror camps in Pakistan and PoK, killing at least 100 terrorists. The Indian Air Force also struck targets at 13 Pakistani airbases and military installations. The nine terror camps hit by Indian forces with a mix of missiles and smart munitions included Markaz Subhanallah in Bahawalpur, Markaz Taiba near Muridke, Mehmoona Joya in Sialkot, Sawai Nala and Syed Na Bilal in Muzaffarabad, Gulpur and Abbas in Kotli, Barnala in Bhimber, and Sarjal.

The IAF hit the targets in Bahawalpur and Muridke; the army hit the rest.

In May 2026, defence minister Rajnath Singh said Operation Sindoor signalled India’s collective resolve and new military ethos, and the “short-duration, deep-penetration, high-intensity, and high-impact operation” compelled Pakistan to surrender. It triggered four days of strikes and counterstrikes with fighter jets, missiles, drones, long-range weapons and heavy artillery before the two sides reached an understanding on stopping all military action on May 10.

Content:
New Delhi: The Congress on Friday attacked the Centre, for not recognising the martyrdom of six soldiers, who laid down their lives during Operation Sindoor, for a year after the Pahalgam terror attack.

Congress leader Pawan Khera said it was a shame that the government that wraps itself in nationalism had denied the heroes the recognition they deserved for a year.

The names of six military personnel -- five from the Indian Army and one from IAF -- who died in the line of duty during Operation Sindoor in May 2025, have been inscribed on a wall at the National War Memorial, as a tribute to the fallen heroes.

In a post on X, Khera named the six personnel and said they are the brave sons of India who laid down their lives defending India’s honour and the sindoor of our sisters after the Pahalgam attack.

“Their names should have been etched into the national consciousness. Their families should have seen a grateful nation honouring their sacrifice.

“Instead, for an entire year, the BJP government chose to conceal their martyrdom from the nation,” the Congress leader said in his post.

“The same government that wraps itself in the flag and speaks endlessly of nationalism denied these heroes the recognition and remembrance they deserved. Such a shame!,” Khera said.

The names inscribed on Wall No. 3D of the Tyag Chakra at the National War Memorial are -- Subedar Major Pawan Kumar, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar, Agniveer Mood Muralinaik, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh from the Army, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar of the Indian Air Force.

The unit names of the personnel have also been inscribed.

Sources said the names were added to the memorial recently and have also been published on the National War Memorial website.

Heading: ‘Misleading and factually incorrect’: Centre hits back as Oppn questions Rajnath Singh’s Op Sindoor remarks
Summary: The Centre has rejected the Opposition's claims regarding Defence Minister Rajnath Singh's statement on Operation Sindoor, calling them "misleading and factually incorrect." The Defence Ministry clarified that Singh's parliamentary remarks, questioned after six jawans were honored, were a specific response to false claims about pilot losses, aimed at countering a narrative that sought to diminish the operation's success. The Centre emphasized that Singh's statement was a proud and accurate account of Operation Sindoor's remarkable success and the Defence Forces' professionalism.
Content:
New Delhi, June 27 (IANS):The Centre has summarily rejected the Opposition’s ‘narrative building exercise’ over Defence Minister Rajnath Singh’s old statement on Operation Sindoor in the Parliament, related to loss of lives in the military exercise, and termed its assertions as “deliberately misleading and factually incorrect.”

The Defence Ministry, taking note of certain social media posts, said that this is a deliberate attempt to “misrepresent” Raksha Mantri’s address delivered on the floor of Parliament on July 28, 2025, by selectively quoting isolated portions of his speech.

The controversy over Rajnath Singh’s statement over ‘no soldiers’ death in the Parliament, days after Operation Sindoor, started after six fallen jawans were immortalised by inscribing their names on the National War Memorial in the capital yesterday. This marked the first public revelation of the names of the armed forces jawans who laid their lives in Operation Sindoor.

This gave the Congress an opportunity to train guns at the Centre and the Defence Minister, as it claimed that the latter tried to gloss over the sacrifice of soldiers during Operation Sindoor, thus not giving them the respect and honour that they deserved.

Congress leader Pawan Khera dug out the old parliamentary address of Rajnath Singh and said that there could be only two possibilities – either the Defence Minister was unaware of the martyrdom of six soldiers while addressing the House, or the other could be that he knew the truth and yet chose to mislead.

He said that both situations raise questions about his competence and added, “This is an insult to our soldiers, and no true patriot can remain silent or complacent about it.”

Another Congress leader, Manish Tewari, targeted the Defence Minister, asking, “Was he oblivious of the facts when he addressed Parliament?”

He said that the Defence Minister, during a debate on Operation Sindoor, said that no harm was caused to any Indian soldier during Operation Sindoor, but then, after 13 months, released the names of six soldiers martyred in the operation.

The Centre, replying to these charges, said that these posts selectively quote a truncated portion of the Defence Minister’s speech to falsely imply that he claimed that no Indian soldier lost his life during Operation Sindoor.

Dismissing the narrative as ‘mischievous’, it said that when the Raksha Mantri made the statement in Parliament, there were multiple claims of India losing its pilots in the operation, and therefore, his remarks should be seen in that context and not otherwise.

“The Union Minister’s remarks were a targeted and contextually specific response to a falsehood that was gaining dangerous traction at that moment,” the Defence Ministry said in a statement.

It also said the narrative was entirely false, yet it was aggressively amplified with the intent to diminish the operation's success and demoralise public sentiment.

It further said that Rajnath Singh’s statement in the Parliament was, in its entirety, a proud and accurate account of the remarkable success of Operation Sindoor, an operation that saw Defence Forces demonstrating unmatched precision, resolve, and military professionalism by hitting multiple targets deep inside Pakistan.

Synopsis:Almost 400 days after Operation Sindoor, India has finally named its fallen heroes.

A year and a little over a month later, the government has officially named the heroes who lost their lives in Operation Sindoor.

The government named six armed forces personnel who made the ultimate sacrifice and whose names will now be engraved upon the ‘Tyag Chakra’ (Circle of Sacrifice) at the National War Memorial in New Delhi.

Five of the personnel were from the Army:

Subedar Major Pawan Kumar – Headquarters, 10 Infantry Brigade Rifleman, from Shahpur in Himachal Pradesh.

Sunil Kumar, Vir Chakra – 4th Battalion of the Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry, from Trewa village in Jammu.

Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar (33) – 5th Field Regiment, from Haryana.

Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh – 237 Field Workshop Company, from Taranagar village in Bihar and honoured earlier this year with the Sena Medal.

Aviation Technician Murali Naik (23) – From Andhra Pradesh and belonging to the 851 Light Regiment (Agniveer from the Indian Army)

The death of Vayu Medal winner Sergeant Surendra Kumar of the 39 Wing of the Indian Air Force was also officially confirmed. He was a medical assistant working with the IAF’s life-support team. He is survived by his wife, mother and young son.

Operation Sindoorhad been launched in response to the terrorist attack in Jammu and Kashmir’s Pahalgam on April 22, 2025, in which 25 Indians and one Nepali citizen were brutally gunned down. India held Pakistan-trained terrorists responsible for the crime and went after terrorist camps and infrastructure.

The Operation began on May 7, 2025 and lasted four days. The conflict had seen drones being employed for the first time by the nuclear-armed neighbours.

Heading: Who is the brave Air Force Sergeant Surendra Moga? Who received honor for his martyrdom in 'Operation Sindoor'

Content:
Rajasthan News: The Ministry of Defense has officially released the names of all 6 jawans martyred in 'Operation Sindoor'. Among them, Sergeant Surendra Moga of Jhunjhunu is the only martyr from the Indian Air Force. After a long dispute, the family said - better late than never, but the son's martyrdom has been honored.

Who Is Sergeant Surendra Moga: Taking a significant step in the history of armed forces policy and national security, the Ministry of Defense has officially made public the names of all 6 brave martyrs who made the supreme sacrifice under 'Operation Sindoor', which includes 5 Army personnel and the sole brave warrior of the Indian Air Force, Sergeant Surendra Moga. With this historic announcement, the dispute that arose last year in July 2025 regarding records and statements within the Parliament has now completely subsided, and these 'unsung heroes' of the country have received their highest national honor. This whole matter escalated when, on July 28, 2025, during the review of 'Operation Sindoor' in the Lok Sabha, Defense Minister Rajnath Singh, in response to a question, inadvertently stated that there was no loss of any soldier in this operation. Expressing deep outrage over this technical and strategic statement, the then MP from Jhunjhunu, Brijendra Ola, strongly demanded a correction of the record in Parliament and stated that Sergeant Surendra Moga, a brave son from his district, was martyred in this very operation. At that time, emotional statements from the martyr's wife Seema Devi and mother Nanu Devi came out through the media, in which Seema Devi said that she did not want anything from the government, only that the martyrdom be given full respect, while mother Nanu Devi said that what could be a greater loss than losing a son.

The dispute came to light in July, then the Air Force Chief visited the village. Immediately after the dispute arose in Parliament at the end of July, in August 2025, Indian Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal Amarpreet Singh himself reached the ancestral home of martyr Surendra Moga and consoled his wife and mother, assuring them that the Air Force would never let its brave warrior's sacrifice go in vain. Subsequently, honoring his indomitable courage for the country, Her Excellency President Droupadi Murmu posthumously awarded Sergeant Moga the prestigious 'Vayu Sena Medal (Gallantry)', and the Air Force permanently named an official wing in New Delhi “Surendra Hall”.

Family said - better late than never, but there is satisfaction. Today, after this glorious defense record and events have been made public, all the villagers of Mehradasi have expressed their deep satisfaction. The martyr Surendra's uncles Pyarelal, Shivchand, brothers Ravi, Sanjeev, Rajesh, becoming emotional, said that even though the lamp of their family has been extinguished forever and this pain can never lessen, today their son's name shines proudly on the national stage. After a long wait, the official recognition and honor given by the government has raised the family's head with pride, and they feel complete satisfaction with this step taken by the country.

The only warrior from the Indian Air Force to make the supreme sacrifice. In this highly confidential and dangerous mission, 'Operation Sindoor', launched to eliminate terrorists across the border, Sergeant Surendra Moga was the only brave warrior from the entire Indian Air Force who made the supreme sacrifice for the country by being deployed on the front line. The valor shown by this lone brave warrior of the Air Force, along with five Army personnel, has become a unique example of joint operations in Indian military history.

The only martyr from the brave land of Rajasthan during the entire operation. Sergeant Surendra Moga, who attained martyrdom during 'Operation Sindoor' from the state of Rajasthan, known as the land of bravery and sacrifice, was the only brave warrior. Sergeant Moga, who emerged from Mehradasi village in Jhunjhunu district and challenged enemies across the border, has given a new sky to the glory of Rajasthan's military tradition. His being the only Rajasthani in this entire operation is a matter of supreme pride not only for his home district but for the entire state.

The fallen personnel include Subedar Major Pawan Kumar of Headquarters 10 Infantry Brigade, Rifleman Sunil Kumar, Vir Chakra, of 4 Jammu and Kashmir Light Infantry, Lance Naik Dinesh Kumar of 5 Field Regiment, Aviation Technician Mood Muralinaik of 851 Light Regiment, Havildar Sunil Kumar Singh of 237 Field Workshop Company and Sergeant Surendra Kumar, Vayu Medal, of 39 Wing.

The names have been engraved on Wall 3D of the memorial in the 2025 section dedicated to military personnel who laid down their lives in service of the nation.

Until now, the government had not officially disclosed the identities of personnel killed during Operation Sindoor, despite reports and speculation about military casualties during the four-day conflict between India and Pakistan in May 2025.

The publication of the names on the National War Memorial's Roll of Honour effectively amounts to the first official confirmation of the armed forces personnel who lost their lives during the operation.

Operation Sindoor was launched in the early hours of May 7, 2025, weeks after the April 22 terror attack in Pahalgam in which 26 civilians, most of them tourists, were killed.

Indian armed forces carried out precision strikes on nine terror-linked sites in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, targeting infrastructure linked to Jaish-e-Mohammed and Lashkar-e-Taiba. India and Pakistan agreed to halt military action on May 10 following talks between the two countries' Directors General of Military Operations.

The newly revealed names indicate that the casualties during Operation Sindoor were spread across the Army and the Indian Air Force, reflecting the joint nature of the military campaign involving coordinated action by multiple services.

Among those honoured is Rifleman Sunil Kumar, who was awarded the Vir Chakra for gallantry, and Sergeant Surendra Kumar, a recipient of the Vayu Medal, highlighting the role played by decorated personnel in the operation.

The National War Memorial, inaugurated in 2019 near India Gate, commemorates Indian armed forces personnel who have died in military operations and conflicts after Independence. The addition of the six names formally places Operation Sindoor among the operations remembered at the memorial.
